articles.title: Rangers 3-2 Aberdeen: Gers beat Dons in five-goal thriller to cut Celtic's Premiership lead to one point
articles.summary: Report as Rangers beat Aberdeen at Ibrox; Brad Lyons gave Aberdeen a surprise lead; Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin hit back after the break; Findlay Marshall fired the Dons back into the game; the Ibrox side are one point behind Premiership leaders Celtic
articles.body:
Derek McInnes' side needed to win their game in hand to cut Celtic's lead at the top of the table, but did not get it all their own way on a rainy night in Govan.

After Dan Neil and Ryan Naderi came close, Aberdeen took a shock lead to silence Ibrox. Nico Raskin thought he had cleared Brad Lyons header, but VAR confirmed the ball was already over the line.

Ivor Pandur's brilliant stop denied Ayoub Mouloua a second for the Dons before a triple half-time change sent the hosts on their way to victory.

Minsu Kim's first involvement resulted in the equaliser as Marius Muller spilled his shot into Ryan Naderi's path and he made no mistake.

Just 65 seconds later, Rangers were in front when Djeidi Gassama fired Naderi's ball into the net. Nico Raskin slotted in a third, but Findlay Marshall's wonderful strike pulled Mario Frick's side back into the game with Pandur pulling off another brilliant stop to make sure the three points stayed in Glasgow.

Rangers can move top of the Premiership on Saturday if they can halt Falkirk's winning run. Aberdeen remain eighth.

2: CLOSE! James Penrice sends in a brilliant cross, but both Dan Neil and Ryan Naderi fail to turn it into the net.

4: CHANCE! Djeidi Gassama makes a brilliant run, then decides to cross the ball to Badredine Bouanani who fails to make contact.

30: OFF THE LINE! Findlay Marshall sends the ball into Brad Lyons. Nico Raskin clears is off the line, but was the ball in?

30: GOAL ABERDEEN! It was over the line and the Dons are in front!

38: SAVE! Almost a second for Aberdeen! Ayoub Mouloua is one-on-one with Ivor Pandur and keeper manages to tip it away.

47: GOAL RANGERS! Marius Muller can't hold on to Minsu Kim's shot. It's straight into Naderi's path and he makes no mistake.

48: GOAL RANGERS! Naderi with the assist this time as he sends a lovely ball to Gassama to fire into the far corner.

56: GOAL RANGERS! Aberdeen are caught on the break. Gassama runs the length of the pitch and sets up Raskin to fire through Muller's legs.

58: GOAL ABERDEEN! Marshall's left-footed strike goes in off the post and the Dons are back in this.

62: SAVE! What a stop from Pandur to stop Aberdeen pulling level as he reacts to stop their corner from hitting the back of the net.

90+3: BIG MISS! For Rangers. Kim pounces on the loose ball, cuts inside to avoid the defender but curls his shot wide of the target.

Boyd: Where would Rangers be without Naderi?

"He's had a goal or an assist in every single game since coming on here against Motherwell when he was out of the team.

"There's been a lot of players who've had plaudits, but where would Rangers be without Naderi?

"A lot of games have been tied and it always seems to be the first, or the goal that puts Rangers ahead, or the goal that seals it.

"He's scored five goals, he can go back to the [League Cup] semi-final, found a way there. Celtic, found a way at Celtic Park to get the ball in the net as well.

"Him and Kelsy didn't really work tonight, but you can understand why Derek left Naderi on the pitch, because he's the one that's assisting, he's the one that's scoring goals, he's always in and around."

Rangers manager Derek McInnes speaking to Sky Sports:

"I thought we only really played with the intelligence, the speed, the intensity for about 20 minutes. In that period, we showed how good we can be, but we put the game at risk.

"But our naivety with the second goal is beyond me, because I'm not sure it was a free-kick in the first place, but that said, we turned back, they allowed the extra man.

"We almost, as if we were in a daydream, allowed them to manipulate the ball and he gets a free shot and a goal.

"Great finish from Marshall, but at the same token, we put ourselves in the mire there with that, just knocking off.

"We were so naive at times in the game tonight, so I'm relieved to win because we will play a lot better this season and maybe not win.

"We've won the game, we've dusted ourselves down, there's loads to get through in that game in terms of analysis.

"But we keep winning and I'm delighted we've won the game. It was three good goals from our point of view and I'm delighted with the impact of the subs and I'm delighted the players dug it out.

"But we made it harder for ourselves and we had to."

Frick confident the 'true Aberdeen' will come

Aberdeen head coach Mario Frick on Sky Sports:

"Disappointed for the result at the end. Knocked out by five or six minutes after half-time.

"We were too naive. We gave them some gifts. It's a pity because we played very well.

"We had some chances and also after 3-1 down, we came back. I think we deserved the equaliser too.

"We are very ambitious. We are very disappointed today. We need more time, more training sessions.

"We have to recover some injured players too.

"We are a good team with a lot of quality and I think in a bit of time we will see the true Aberdeen."

articles.title: Latest Bowl Projections, 2026 CFP Playoff Bracket Scenarios and Week 13 Predictions
articles.summary: The 2026 college football season has been defined by its surprising finishes and outcomes. Week 12 brought more of the same, as UCLA fell from the ranks of the unbeaten, and Indiana had its playoff hopes dashed in Seattle.
articles.body:
The 2026 college football season has been defined by its surprising finishes and outcomes. Week 12 brought more of the same, as UCLA fell from the ranks of the unbeaten, and Indiana had its playoff hopes dashed in Seattle.

While the College Football Playoff (CFP) selection committee won't release its latest rankings until Tuesday evening, the AP rankings dropped on Sunday and should provide some idea of the still-developing playoff picture.

Things could change again in Week 13. Here, we'll dive into the latest rankings, examine the most pivotal matchup on the upcoming schedule, and make some CFP bracket predictions.

The Demon Deacons continued their march toward the CFP with a lopsided win over Georgia Tech. Wake Forest locked up a spot in the ACC title game with the victory and will face Miami on Saturday, December 5.

Winning the ACC Championship would guarantee Wake Forest a spot in the CFP, as all four Power Four conference champs will earn automatic bids. However, a close loss to the Hurricanes should still leave the Demon Deacons in the playoff field.

Despite a close loss to Ohio State several weeks ago, the Hoosiers appeared headed toward another CFP appearance. The defending champs hadn't been as dominant as they were a year ago, but they still appeared capable of doing damage in the playoff.

All of that changed on Sunday, though, as the Huskies pulled out an overtime win over Curt Cignetti's squad. Indiana can still get in by reaching the Big Ten title game and earning an automatic berth. However, it currently resides in a position to give way to the top Group of Six champion in the playoff field.

UCLA was also upset in Week 12, which ended the Bruins' undefeated streak. Losing to a very inconsistent Michigan squad definitely hurt the credibility of Bob Chesney's squad, and everything may now come down to the Big Ten title game.

A win over USC this week will guarantee UCLA a spot in the conference championship—most likely in a matchup with Oregon or Indiana. That's huge for the Bruins, as it now appears that only one Big Ten team will make the playoff this year.

Schedule: Thursday, November 26 at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN

This is a massive game for Texas Tech, which entered the week on the CFP fringe. The Red Raiders are now in a much more favorable spot, though they'll need a win over TCU to secure a berth in the Big-12 title game.

A loss here would open the door for BYU.

Schedule: Saturday, November 28 at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS

As previously mentioned, UCLA can secure a spot in the Big Ten Championship by beating the cross-town Trojans. The Bruins are expected to do just that, though USC is no stranger to the spoiler's role.

Schedule: Saturday, November 28 at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC

This week is also huge for the Ducks, who appeared to be out of CFP contention just a few days ago. Indiana's loss gives Oregon life, and a win over the team that just beat the Hoosiers will get the Ducks in.

However, a loss would reopen the door for Indiana, which needs two losses from the group of UCLA, Oregon, and Iowa to sneak into the title game.

Schedule: Saturday, November 28 at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC

Alabama appears headed to the CFP regardless of Saturday's outcome in the Iron Bowl. The Crimson Tide are ratings gold and would probably get forced in by the committee, even with three losses.

However, a win would leave the door open for an SEC title game appearance and cement Kalen DeBoer's team as a top-tier playoff contender. The Tide have several quality wins this season and can earn another one against an Auburn squad that previously upset the top-ranked Georgia Bulldogs.

articles.title: Leny Yoro red card: Manchester United defender cleared to face Brentford on Saturday
articles.summary: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro is clear to face Brentford on Saturday as his red card at Anfield is overturned.
articles.body:
Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card shown to him at Anfield overturned by the Football Association - even though referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.

Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into Sunday's match.

Isak had run onto a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought down the Swede.

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at a decision he felt had changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.

"The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.

"But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul."

The FA backed that view, meaning Yoro will be clear to face Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, in the latest edition of Mic'd Up on Sky Sports, Webb said Barrott got it right.

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," he said.

'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?

How can a decision be both right and wrong?

How on earth can the head of referees say a decision was right, but the FA say it was wrong?

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable," Webb said. "Certainly not clearly wrong."

Not clearly and obviously wrong for a VAR intervention, but clearly and obviously wrong for the FA to rescind the red card.

You wonder how the general fan is supposed to understand it all.

The FA's appeals process is notoriously difficult to predict, especially on highly borderline situations like Yoro.

A commission features three people, usually former players though sometimes there is a retired official is on the panel.

A simple majority is needed, so a club just needs two people to agree with them.

It's why clubs might appeal against red cards when it seems impossible to win, you just never know.

Such was the split of opinion on Yoro, United always stood a chance of at least getting those key two votes.

And this is the crux of appeals process. An FA commission is just the subjective opinion of three people.

Do the appeal again tomorrow with three different panel members, and United might lose.

This is why Pro Ref don't use the outcome of FA appeals to determine how games are officiated.

Two years ago, Brentford's Christian Norgaard won an appeal against a red card at Everton. That was a split 2:1 vote, but enough to say a decision was wrong.

Pro Ref told its referees not to alter their interpretation based on this vote.

Let's throw in another one. The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel.

Earlier this season, Brighton appealed against Pascal Struijk's VAR red card at Sunderland.

An FA commission upheld the appeal, but in contradiction the KMI Panel voted the VAR intervention was correct.

Make it make sense, supporters might ask.

This will forever be the problem with officiating, and indeed any hope of true consistency with VAR.

Was Yoro's red card right or wrong? On which side of the fence will the KMI Panel fall?

Football is just a floating mass of subjectivity. Of referees, of VARs, of panel members and of fans. It just depends whose opinion you ask.

Sporting boss Fonseca dismisses Man Utd fragile talk

United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT).

The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break.

But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile".

"I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon.

"Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma.

"Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day."

United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions.

Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect.

"Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said.

"I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict."

articles.title: Couple Addresses Viral Video of 'Argument' Narrated by Jesse Palmer During WF-Georgia Tech Game
articles.summary: The couple whose conversation during last Saturday's game between No. 11 Wake Forest and Georgia Tech was narrated by Jesse Palmer say their argument was centered around a "miscommunication."
articles.body:
The couple whose conversation during last Saturday's game between No. 11 Wake Forest and Georgia Tech was narrated by Jesse Palmer say their argument was centered around a "miscommunication."

Georgia Tech students Tallulah Wall and Braden Flournoy talked about their viral discussion in a Tuesday appearance on the Today Show .

"To clear the air, there was zero speculation between us about breaking up," Flournoy said, per Scott Stump of Today.com.

The talk between the Georgia Tech students was initially broken down by Palmer and analyst Joe Tessitore during ESPN's broadcast of Wake Forest's 50-29 win.

"A lot of our friends actually had no idea we were dating until that happened," Flournoy told Savannah Guthrie, Jenna Bush Hager and Craig Melvin, per Stump.

"So not only were we getting texts, 'Oh hey, you were on the screen for like a solid couple seconds,' it was, 'You have a boyfriend?'" Wall said, per Stump.

Wake Forest will now hope Saturday's win was enough to help the Demon Deacons climb the College Football Playoff standings when the selection committee's next rankings drop Tuesday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Debbie Hewitt signs NDA after viewing documents on failed Fifa sell-off plot
articles.summary: Debbie Hewitt is among several football chiefs to view documents made available by Fifa, but cannot speak about them.
articles.body:
Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) as a condition of viewing documents related to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.

Hewitt was granted access to the information at the world governing body's headquarters in Zurich.

Earlier this month, Fifa said "key documents" on the abandoned plan to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors would be made available to members of its council, but only in person and under "strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality".

Uefa had demanded Fifa release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and answer questions relating to its decision-making.

Hewitt was among a group of council members who wrote to Fifa to say they were "concerned that any review would seemingly be limited to certain 'key documents'… which in turn would only be available for review under unknown 'strict review protocols'".

They also asked for clarity on what the protocols were, and "an explanation as to why Fifa considers such restrictions necessary since it is not clear why our rights are being limited in such a way".

The NDA means Hewitt cannot reveal what she has read, or comment about it publicly.

Fair Square, which campaigns for greater accountability in sport, told BBC Sport: "Debbie Hewitt and the FA didn't need to see the details of FFE to know that it was a gross abuse of presidential power.

"As a member association, the FA is entitled to hold the Fifa president accountable for his actions, and as a Fifa Council vice-president, Hewitt should have seen these plans as soon as they were hatched.

"They had the right to demand to see these documents, and should have exercised that right forcefully and publicly, rather than signing a gagging clause that puts Fifa and Infantino back in control."

115 days, 39 private-jet flights, one election - Infantino's globetrotting

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling

Hewitt has previously criticised Infantino for a lack of transparency.

However, she embraced the Fifa president at a ceremony in Zurich on Monday when the UK bid to host the 2035 Women's World Cup was ratified at a special ceremony.

It is unclear whether she viewed the files on the same day, and which documents have been made available.

Last week, BBC Sport revealed the FA had considered challenging Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, and that it is backing French candidate Philippe Diallo in next year's presidential election.

Fifa has been approached for comment. Sources have previously indicated Fifa's ability to answer some questions is limited by legal action that Uefa launched in October in the US, requesting disclosure of evidence and documents, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

articles.title: El Madrid no remata un gran espectáculo de goles y fútbol
articles.standfirst: El PSV aguanta casi media hora en inferioridad tras plantar cara en igualdad a los blancos, que se mantienen invictos y tienen el 'top 6' casi asegurado
articles.summary: El PSV aguanta casi media hora en inferioridad tras plantar cara en igualdad a los blancos, que se mantienen invictos y tiene el 'top 6' casi asegurado
articles.body: No pudo ser la quinta victoria, esa que suponía hacer pleno en este camino a reeditar el título europeo y que hubiera asegurado al juvenil de Álvaro López, con una jornada de adelanto, la clasificación en el ‘top 6’. Fue un empate, que deja el objetivo casi conseguido, ante un gran PSV liderado por un estelar Hansen, autor de tres dianas. El resultado, un gran espectáculo de fútbol y goles que el Madrid, con la conexión Ciria-Yáñez desatada, no pudo rematar con el triunfo tras jugar casi media hora en superioridad. El PSV que arrancó con personalidad, empezó adelantándose por medio de su delantero, Hansen, que acabaría protagonizando un triplete. Los de Álvaro López supieron reaccionar para empatar a los pocos minutos, con el tanto de Ciria tras el pase de Yáñez. Sería el gaditano quien, minutos después y en una gran jugada personal, sellara la remontada provisional con un fenomenal disparo desde el costado diestro. Cuando parecía tener el equipo blanco tenía el encuentro controlado, llegó el golazo de Hansen de falta directa, que no se conformó con eso y volvió a batir al debutante Álvaro Rodríguez, esta vez de una bonita espuela, de nuevo resolviendo jugada a balón parado. Un doble golpe justo antes del descanso para que los visitantes se marcharan ganando. En la reanudación los holandeses volvieron a salir fuertes, pero los de Álvaro López siguieron trabajando para superar la calidad del rival e igualar el resultado. Pasada la hora del encuentro, Fran Santamaría logró perforar la puerta del PSV tras la asistencia atrás del capitán Carlos Díez. Los madridistas siguieron percutiendo e intensificaron su ataque aprovechando la expulsión de Buyens en el 65’, pero el larguero se alió con los de Eindhoven para evitar el tanto al chut de Yáñez en el 73’. El carrusel de cambios de Álvaro López buscó volcar en ataque a los suyos y las llegadas se sucedieron, aunque sin la claridad suficiente. En el último instante el meta del PSV despejó el remate a bocajarro de Fran Santamaría en un final de acoso a la meta holandesa. La próxima jornada, en su visita a la casa del Arsenal, se resolverá la posición final de esta fase Liga. articles.title: Liverpool news: Jurgen Klopp advice and Andoni Iraola confidence helps turn Florian Wirtz's form around
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz opens up on why it's the best he has felt since joining Liverpool.
articles.body:
Florian Wirtz says he is enjoying his best form yet at Liverpool and benefiting from Andoni Iraola's confidence and Jurgen Klopp's advice.

Wirtz, 23, scored in Liverpool's 4-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday and has three goals and six assists this season.

The Germany midfielder made the £116m move from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025 and after failing to make his mark in his first campaign in England, is beginning to showcase his quality for Iraola's side.

Speaking in Belgium before Liverpool 's Champions League game against Club Brugge, Wirtz said: "I can't really say that I've changed that much.

"I've become a bit better on a physical level and that's the only reason that could explain it."

He also said he has been picking the brains of Germany manager Klopp, the former Liverpool boss, while on international duty.

"He tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here and tries to give me some advice to get successful over here as he has shown how it is done," Wirtz said.

"He can give me some good advice. It's always small things. More private things.

"But he is speaking good about the club, the region, the people, and that helps to hear someone who has experienced it for a long time."

On the influence of Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot as Liverpool head coach in the summer, Wirtz added: "He is bringing me back in a place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football, and I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I'm really happy about that.

"I'm just trying to give him back what he gives me."

Liverpool have nine points from their four Champions League games, having won their first three before losing to Fenerbahce in Istanbul this month.

Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch are both absent from the travelling squad with injuries, with Iraola confirming that Gakpo will be out for the Merseyside derby this weekend, while adding that it is "difficult to say" for Gravenberch.

articles.title: Yáñez da otro impulso a su leyenda en la Youth League
articles.standfirst: Iguala ante el PSV el récord histórico de partidos en la competición, los 28 de Pedro Álvaro (Benfica)
articles.summary: Iguala ante el PSV el récord histórico de partidos en la competición, los 28 de Pedro Álvaro (Benfica)
articles.body: Hacer historia con 19 años está al alcance de unos pocos privilegiados. Y de ese selecto club forma parte Dani Yáñez. El extremo del Castilla alcanzó este martes ante el PSV los 28 partidos de Pedro Álvaro en la Youth League, récord absoluto de participaciones en la competición. A partir esta jornada, Yáñez ya estará en disposición de apoderarse de él en solitario. Un registro que, como mínimo, podría elevarlo hasta los 30 partidos, porque queda un partido de la fase Liga (Arsenal) y el Madrid está ya clasificado para los dieciseisavos de final. Está siendo una edición de la Youth muy especial para Yáñez, que lleva varias jornadas disfrutando de acontecimientos históricos en la competición. Ante el Leipzig se convirtió en el canterano del Real Madrid con más partidos disputados en la Youth League, 26, superando los 25 de Óscar Rodríguez. Ante el AEK asaltaría la segunda posición en el ranking de comparecencias en la 'Champions' juvenil y ante el PSV igualó los 28 partidos de Pedro Álvaro (Benfica), la cima del torneo hasta el momento. Una cumbre que Yáñez puede colocar bastante más arriba. Es la cuarta temporada de Yáñez en la Youth League. El joven extremo debutó en la competición a las órdenes de Arbeloa en la edición 23-24, jugando su primer partido el 20 de septiembre de 2023 ante el Unión Berlín. Aquella temporada jugaría seis partidos y marcaría un gol. En la 24-25 jugó los ocho partidos del Madrid en la Youth, hasta que cayó en los octavos de final, marcando cuatro goles. La pasada temporada, la última como juvenil, tocó el cielo continental conquistando una Youth en la que disputó nueve partidos, marcó dos goles y dio una asistencia. En esta nueva temporada, la cuarta y la última de Yáñez en la 'Champions juvenil', el extremo la juega como uno de los cinco jugadores nacidos en 2007 que cada club puede inscribir. De momento, cinco partidos, cinco goles y dos asistencias. En total, el balance de Yáñez en la Youth es de 28 partidos, 12 goles, seis asistencias y un título. Yáñez es leyenda de la Champions juvenil, pero aún no ha tocado techo. Entre otras cosas porque también tiene a tiro ser el máximo goleador de la competición. El extremo lleva 12 goles desde su estreno en la 23-24 y el récord está en los 15 tantos que consiguieron Charlie Brown (Chelsea), Borja Mayoral (Real Madrid) y Roberto Núñez (Atlético de Madrid).

articles.title: OSU's Jeremiah Smith Headlines Maxwell & Biletnikoff Finalists, Full List of Contenders Announced
articles.summary: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith could cap off his historic junior season by winning multiple end-of-season awards.
articles.body:
Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith could cap off his historic junior season by winning multiple end-of-season awards.

Smith was announced Tuesday as a finalist for both the Biletnikoff Award, which recognizes the top receiver in the FBS, and the Maxwell Award, which honors "the most outstanding player in college football."

NFL Teams That Could Trade Up for Jeremiah Smith 📈

Oregon State's Jesse Legree and Miami's Malachi Toney are also finalists for the Biletnikoff Award, while Miami's Darian Mensah and Utah's Devon Dampier joined Smith as finalists for the Maxwell Award.

The news comes days after Smith became the first wide receiver in Big Ten history to rack up 4,000 career receiving yards in last Saturday's upset loss to Nebraska.

Although the Buckeyes have fallen out of playoff contention since losing Julian Sayin to a throwing-arm injury, Smith has remained on track to lead the FBS in major receiving stats this season.

Smith has topped 100 receiving yards in each of his last three games while working with true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey and is heading into this weekend's regular season finale with an FBS-high 1,482 receiving yards and 17 touchdown catches.

That ranks just ahead of Legree, who has racked up 1,418 receiving yards and 15 touchdown catches with Oregon State.

Toney has been sidelined since Oct. 31 after suffering a high ankle sprain necessitating surgery, but he is still tied for fourth in the FBS with 13 touchdown catches to go along with 1,027 receiving yards in eight games.

That run from Toney took place in part thanks to Mensah, who leads the FBS with a 75.4 percent completion percentage. Despite throwing a season-high two interceptions in last Saturday's win over Virginia Tech, Mensah still boasts season-long stats of 3,317 passing yards alongside 29 touchdowns and just four picks.

Dampier has kept Utah on track for a College Football Playoff bid while completing 66.3 percent of his passes with 2,535 yards and 24 touchdowns to eight interceptions.

These players will get one more shot at making their case for end-of-season awards, including the Heisman Trophy ahead of the Dec. 7 voting deadline and finalists announcement, when closing out the regular season this week.

Ohio State is slated to play Michigan, while Miami faces Boston College, Oregon State plays at Fresno State and Utah hosts West Virginia during Rivalry Week.

Muuuuuuuuuuy buenas tardeeeeeeees. Champions en el Bernabéu , así que noche bonita. El PSV visita a un Real Madrid intratable en la competición y en su estadio. articles.title: El Valencia, última víctima del arbitraje en la Liga F
articles.standfirst: Un penalti no pitado, una expulsión y dos futbolistas lesionadas
articles.summary: Un penalti no pitado, una expulsión y dos futbolistas lesionadas
articles.body: Pocos se imaginaban en el Valencia que en el día después de su partido contra el Espanyol iba a haber una mezcla de indignación y tristeza. La actuación de Beatriz Cuesta y del videoarbitraje desesperó a jugadoras, cuerpo técnico y aficionados valencianistas que todavía siguen mostrando su enfado por lo sucedido. Dos acciones claves están suponiendo un aluvión de críticas tras el partido: el penalti no pitado a Yasmin con posterior expulsión de la mediocentro valencianista y la entrada temeraria de Mar Torras a Wifi en el tramo final del encuentro. La sucesión de hechos comienzan con una dudosa mano de Ari Domènech dentro del área perica que termina siendo señalada como penalti. El balón impacta en el brazo pero la futbolista está girada y lo tiene bastante pegado al cuerpo. Yasmin no logra transformar la pena máxima aunque marca el rechace, pero Beatriz Cuesta decide no dar el gol entendiendo que Meritxell Muñoz lo tenía agarrado con las manos. Es entonces cuando llega la jugada clave que marcará el partido. En un centro desde la parte derecha del Valencia la propia Yasmin recibe el impacto del codo de Browne en la cara mientras otra futbolista del Espanyol le agarra para impedir que salte a por el balón. La mediocentro valencianista cae al césped, se echa rápidamente la mano a la nariz y la árbitra decide no señalar nada. Cuesta acude al vídeo arbitraje y decide no pitar el penalti ante la incredulidad del banquillo valencianista y la propia Yasmin. La internacional marroquí, con la mano en la cara y sangre en la nariz debido al codazo recibido lanza una botella que no impacta con la árbitra. Beatriz decide sacarle la tarjeta roja y expulsarla. La situación más grave y que más entristece al vestuario llegó en los últimos compases del encuentro. Con el tiempo ya cumplido y con dos a cero en el marcador. Mar Torras protagoniza una entrenada temeraria sobre Lucia Moral ‘Wifi’. Sin posibilidad de jugar el balón, la futbolista del Espanyol le pega en la zona del tobillo a la delantera del Valencia cuando esta corría con el balón desde su propio campo sin que esto supusiera una opción de peligro . Tras un mal gesto provocado por la entrada, Wifi se hace daño en la rodilla y tiene que abandonar el terreno de luego en camilla. Durante este martes la cordobesa se ha sometido a varias pruebas médicas que le dirán el alcance de una lesión que se puede convertir en importante. La colegiada entendió que la entrada no era expulsión y tan solo le mostró la tarjeta amarilla. Pero el Valencia no es el único equipo afectado por un bajo nivel arbitral que se repite temporada tras temporada. Hay varios ejemplos vividos en la presente campaña que han despertado multitud de protestas. Desde el excesivo tiempo de prolongación en el Deportivo-Barça a las protestas del propio conjunto catalán en un penalti no señalado y que parecía claro frente a la Real Sociedad. Todavía levanta ampollas en Tenerife el posible fuera de juego no señalado en uno de los goles del Real Madrid. En este último caso, ni siquiera la cámara mostró la posición de la futbolista madridista.

articles.title: El mensaje de Tebas tras la dimisión de Gil Marín como vicepresidente de LaLiga
articles.standfirst: Agradece al consejero delegado del Atlético durante su etapa en la patronal y celebra la aprobación de presupuestos y las cuentas tras la Asamblea General
articles.summary: Agradece al consejero delegado del Atlético durante su etapa en la patronal y celebra la aprobación de presupuestos y las cuentas tras la Asamblea General
articles.body: El presidente de LaLiga, Javier Tebas, ha publicado un mensaje en sus redes sociales tras conocerse durante la tarde de este martes la dimisión de Miguel Ángel Gil Marín como vicepresidente de la patronal. Un mensaje de agradecimiento y de celebración por la aprobación de las cuentas y el presupuesto en la Asamblea General Ordinaria. "Los clubes han vuelto a respaldar con claridad la gestión de LALIGA. La amplísima mayoría con la que han aprobado las cuentas y el presupuesto en la Asamblea General Ordinaria nos da impulso para seguir trabajando unidos y hacer crecer el fútbol profesional español como venimos haciendo", comienza diciendo Tebas. Además de recordar que Rafael Louzán, presidente de la RFEF, ha estado presente, ha querido agradecer su labor a Gil Marín. "Mi agradecimiento a Miguel Ángel Gil Marín por su labor como vicepresidente primero de LALIGA y por todos estos años de colaboración", expresó. Los motivos de la renuncia del consejero delegado del Atlético estarían relacionados con el malestar generado entre distintos clubes por la financiación por parte de LaLiga de la Unión de Clubes Europeos (UEC), una asociación constituida en 2023 para defender los intereses de los clubes europeos, especialmente los de pequeño y mediano tamaño, y que nació como alternativa a la entonces ECA, actualmente denominada EFC. Según las informaciones a las que ha tenido acceso MARCA, Javier Tebas habría reconocido la pasada semana ante los clubes que LaLiga llevaba años financiando e impulsando esta organización. Una aportación económica que podría superar el millón de euros y de la que, presuntamente, no habrían tenido conocimiento los clubes. El malestar habría aumentado tras conocerse que la UEC habría presentado una denuncia ante la Comisión Europea contra la UEFA y la EFC, asociación de la que forman parte numerosos clubes españoles. Se daría así la circunstancia de que algunos de estos clubes estarían financiando indirectamente, a través de LaLiga, una acción legal contra una organización a la que ellos mismos pertenecen. Varios clubes españoles estarían estudiando ya las implicaciones jurídicas de esta situación, tanto por el destino de los fondos de LaLiga como por el procedimiento seguido para financiar a la UEC.

articles.body: El día a día de Alex Padilla en el Athletic está marcado por Unai Simón. El elegido como mejor portero del mundo le cierra el paso hacia la titularidad de un Athletic al que Padilla sólo ha podido defender desde el campo en la primera eliminatoria de Copa. El internacional por México confía en repetir dentro de una semana frente al Numancia en la eliminatoria que llevará a los dieciseisavos de final de la competición. El zarauztarra ha señalado que “soy el compañero del mejor portero del mundo así que no hay mejor compañero para aprender, para crecer, para pedirle consejos, para escucharle, para trabajar en el día a día y para competir. Para mí es un privilegio estar con Simón”. El portero (23 años) tiene contrato hasta 2029 y tener por delante a Simón convierte en muy complicado la posibilidad de contar con minutos. Ni le incomoda ni bajará los brazos por ello. “Yo sé que estoy preparado para cuando el equipo me necesite. Trabajo día a día para estar a mi mejor nivel y si el míster me necesita en cualquier momento, ayudar al equipo”, añadió. El portero, internacional con México, y Bibiane Schulze, futbolista del femenino y biznieta de Patxo Belauste, ha sido protagonista en el Museo Athletic de la inaguración de la exposición Entre México y Bilbao. Historias compartidas de fútbol. La exposición temporal reconstruye a través del fútbol una parte de la historia que ha unido a los pueblos mexicano y vasco. La muestra se estrenó el pasado junio en el marco de la Copa Mundial de Futbol 2026, exhibiéndose de manera simultánea en los museos Vizcaínas y Arozena de México.

articles.title: Galatasaray 1-0 Aston Villa: Deniz Gul's late winner in Champions League league phase extends Villa's winless run
articles.summary: Match report as Deniz Gul's strike beats Aston Villa in the Champions League league phase, with Galatasaray winning 1-0; the game lacked chances, with Villa failing to score for a second game in a row; Unai Emery's side have not won in six matches
articles.body:
It is the first time Villa have lost back-to-back league phase or group games under Unai Emery, putting them in a perilous position ahead of tough games against PSG and Borussia Dortmund in their next two European fixtures.

The Premier League side have not won since beating Manchester City on October 24, and have not scored since Leon Goretzka's strike against Manchester United on November 8.

It was a game that lacked chances, and it took until the 79th minute - Gul's goal - for a shot on target. Villa failed to deal with a corner, with Nicolas Jackson's poor attempted clearance landing to the Galatasaray forward, who nodded home for his first Champions League goal.

He took a boot to the face from Jackson with the Villa forward attempting to clear. There was a VAR check for a possible red card, but nothing was given.

In contrast to Emery's side, Galatasaray extend their winning run to eight games in all competitions ahead of the Istanbul derby against Besiktas on Monday. They move up to 13th in the league phase table, and have now won three successive Champions League games - matching a club record.

Aston Villa dropped into ninth by the end of Tuesday's matches on goal difference and could do so further by the end of matchday five. They play away to Ipswich next, live on Saturday Night Football.

Emery 'disappointed' and says pitch made it 'difficult'

"Disappointed a little bit. After their goal, it was impossible to play. They wasted time. They added only five minutes. OK. Finish the match. We don't want to play more. I don't think the referee was fair there. It is like that.

"Two years ago we lost to Brugge and Monaco away. Today I can compare this match like those matches.

"Why? Because their supporters are pushing so much. The pitch was not helping. The match was difficult because they pressed intense.

"We did a fantastic job in the first half. We stopped them from keeping the ball and going long. We avoided transitions. It was not enough because we lacked offensively."

"You can be forgiven for losing away at Galatasaray. They have beaten the last four English opponents to travel to their stadium, but it was the performance that will worry Unai Emery.

"It was a similar story to the 0-0 against Sunderland. Villa had more possession than their opponents but struggled to create anything in the final third.

"They have the players to do so. Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson, John McGinn and others are all capable of match-winning moments.

"But for some reason, since conceding two late goals to draw against Manchester United, Villa look lost for ideas in the final third.

"Successive defeats in the Champions League and the previous hold they had within the top eight of the table slipping away is a worry.

"But the real concern should lie with addressing this newfound crisis of confidence in the final third.

"It's Ipswich up next and that will likely be another game where they are given the majority share of possession and are tasked with breaking down a defence.

"At the minute, that feels like a mountain to climb against any opponent."

23: OFFSIDE! Nicolas Jackson finds Johan Manzambi with a cute pass, which the latter fires straight at Cakur. However, the flag is up after.

32: CLOSE! Yunus Akgun delivers a great cross, but no one can convert.

52: CONFRONTATION! John McGinn and Aleksey Batrakov square up after the Villa captain barged the Galatasaray forward to the floor. It came after a reckless high challenge from Davinson Sanchez on Alysson.

64: CLOSE! Gul nods the ball back into the box after a great cross in, but Villa clear.

79: GOAL! Gul nods home after some poor defending from Villa, as VAR checks and clears a possible red card for Jackson.

articles.title: Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham among stars who reportedly visit hospitalised Bayern midfielder Jamal Musiala following two on-pitch collapses in August
articles.summary: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala faces health challenges with neurological conditions, prompting visits from stars like Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham as he awaits medical assessments.
articles.body: Jamal Musiala’s latest health setback has left the Bayern Munich midfielder awaiting further medical assessments after a neurological condition caused two on-pitch collapses in the space of four days and a reported relapse during training this month. As questions grow over his recovery and future at Bayern, Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, Hugo Ekitike and Michael Olise have reportedly visited him in hospital, offering support away from the public debate surrounding his performances and contract.Haaland, Bellingham, Ekitike and Olise visit Musiala in hospitalErling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, Hugo Ekitike and Michael Olise have reportedly visited Jamal Musiala in a German hospital, where the Bayern Munich midfielder is awaiting the results of medical tests.The reported gesture brought together four high-profile players from across European football, with Haaland representing Manchester City, Bellingham Real Madrid, Ekitike Liverpool, and Olise Bayern Munich. Having all spent time playing in Germany across different spells, whether as former Bundesliga rivals or current teammates, the quartet came together in a show of support for Musiala. According to GOAL, their visit gave him a considerable morale boost as he continues to deal with a neurological condition that has interrupted his playing career.The 23-year-old has temporarily stepped away from football after experiencing another setback. Spanish radio station Cadena SER, citing a source close to the Germany international, reported that Musiala has been feeling considerable pressure from the public discussion surrounding his form, salary and future at Bayern.The same source said the midfielder wants to concentrate on his treatment and recovery rather than become involved in arguments over his performances or contract. His hospitalisation comes after two collapses during Bayern's pre-season friendlies in August and a further relapse during a training session in November.Two collapses in four days: what happened to Musiala?Musiala's condition became a major concern during Bayern's pre-season programme in August, when he collapsed twice within four days.The first incident occurred on August 15, during Bayern's 3-1 friendly victory over RB Leipzig. Musiala suddenly appeared unsteady before falling to the pitch, prompting teammate Ismael Saibari to rush over and help him as Bayern's medical staff entered the field.The midfielder appeared dazed but was able to walk off. He recovered sufficiently to return to training shortly afterwards, and the episode initially appeared to have been a temporary setback.Three days later, on August 18, Musiala collapsed again during Bayern's 4-2 friendly win over 1. FC Heidenheim. He had entered the match as a second-half substitute in the 61st minute, but went down around eight minutes later.Players from both teams immediately formed a protective circle around him to shield him from cameras while medical staff treated him on the pitch. Musiala was visibly dazed as he was helped off and replaced.Following the second incident, Musiala addressed his condition in a statement on Instagram, revealing that he had been diagnosed with a neurological dysfunction causing brief absence seizures.He described them as “brief, temporary, but treatable absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction”.Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl subsequently confirmed that the two episodes had occurred after doctors adjusted Musiala's medication for his pre-existing condition. The medication change was therefore identified as a factor in the August incidents, rather than the diagnosis itself being new.There was further concern in November when reports from German media said Musiala had suffered another seizure during a training session. The reported relapse led to further adjustments to his medication and hospital evaluations.German newspaper Bild has also reported that a change in medication triggered episodes similar to those experienced previously, with the recurrence affecting his performances. Musiala is now awaiting the latest medical assessments, with no confirmed timetable for his return to football.Bayern contract debate draws FIFPRO responseMusiala's health problems have unfolded alongside a contentious discussion about his position at Bayern Munich.Club honorary president Uli Hoeness has publicly questioned whether the midfielder's current performances justify his reported annual salary of €25 million. Former Bayern chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has also made comments interpreted as suggesting Musiala could leave the club.The remarks prompted criticism in Germany, particularly because they came while the player was dealing with recurring medical problems. Cadena SER's source close to Musiala said the discussion surrounding his future and contract had added to the pressure he was already experiencing.There have also been reports about a possible change to his agreement. Süddeutsche Zeitung has claimed that a verbal understanding exists to amend the contract in Bayern's favour if Musiala's recovery does not progress as expected. Reports from England have suggested Hoeness is fully aware of the midfielder's medical condition.FIFPRO, the international federation representing professional footballers, responded to the public debate by calling for any contractual concerns to be handled privately with Musiala and his representatives.In a statement, the organisation said:“Turning Musiala's health and future into a public debate only adds to the pressure on him. Any concerns about his contract should be addressed privately with him and his representatives. Contracts are there to be respected.”FIFPRO also rejected the suggestion that a player's injury or decline in form should provide grounds for a club to revisit an existing agreement.It added that “injury or a dip in form does not give a club justification to revisit previously agreed terms, just as a run of outstanding performances does not automatically entitle a player to a pay rise.”The intervention brought further attention to the disagreement over how Bayern's hierarchy has discussed Musiala's situation publicly, while the player remains focused on his health.From Chelsea academy prospect to Bayern's 71-goal midfielderMusiala joined Bayern Munich from Chelsea's academy in July 2019, aged 16, after spending most of his youth career in England. Born in Stuttgart on February 26, 2003, he moved to England with his family when he was seven, spending a year at Southampton before joining Chelsea in 2011.He spent eight years in Chelsea's academy before choosing to return to Germany and join Bayern's youth set-up. His progress through the club's under-17 and under-19 teams was rapid, and he made his senior Bundesliga debut in June 2020, aged 17.Musiala has since become one of Bayern's most important attacking players, recording 71 goals in 236 first-team appearances across all competitions, alongside two goals in 10 appearances for Bayern Munich II. He has also scored 10 goals in 46 senior appearances for Germany.His honours with Bayern include six Bundesliga titles, two DFB-Pokal trophies and five German Super Cups. He was also part of the side that won the Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup during the club's 2019-20 treble and subsequent sextuple-winning period. His tally stands at 16 major trophies with the club.Internationally, Musiala shared the Golden Boot at Euro 2024 after scoring three goals in the tournament. His development into a central figure for Bayern and Germany has made the uncertainty surrounding his health particularly concerning for both sides.For now, the focus is on the results of his medical assessments and whether the latest treatment adjustments can prevent further episodes. The reported visit from Haaland, Bellingham, Ekitike and Olise has offered him support from fellow professionals, but his return to the pitch will depend on his recovery.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Zarpazo' del Galatasaray al Aston Villa
articles.standfirst: El tanto de Deniz Gül en el tramo final del choque le otorgó el triunfo al conjunto otomano
articles.summary: El tanto de Deniz Gül en el tramo final del choque le otorgó el triunfo al conjunto otomano
articles.body: El Aston Villa se ha sumergido en un pequeño bache desde el triunfo contra el Manchester City. Ha transcurrido un mes de aquello y, desde entonces, enlazan seis partidos sin conocer la victoria. Visitar al Galatasaray nunca es plato de buen gusto... y la derrota en Estambul les sacará fuera del Top-8. Las bajas de Rafa Leao y Osimhen condicionaron la propuesta de un Okan Buruk que dobló lateral por izquierda con Jakobs y Elmali. Baris Yilmaz, multiusos, se ubicó como '9' por delante de Batrakov, sensación en Champions. Emery, por su parte, dejó en el banquillo a Pau Torres y, sin Cash, ubicó a Harwood-Bellis como lateral derecho. Alysson, además, sentó a Emi Buendía. El Galatasaray saltó con la intención de entregarle la iniciativa al Aston Villa con el objetivo de juntarse más cerca de su área y hacerse fuerte. Pero, con el paso de los minutos, los turcos fueron elevando el nivel de intensidad y subiendo metros en la presión. Sobre todo, impulsados por el siempre ensordecedor ambiente del RAMS Park. El Aston Villa comenzó a encontrar bastantes dificultades para progresar. Galatasaray juntaba mucha gente por dentro y no conseguía conectar entre líneas con McGinn o Manzambi. Alysson, además, estaba bien controlado por derecha. De hecho, apenas conectaron dos remates en toda la primera parte... y ninguno de ellos le obligó a intervenir a Çakir. Tampoco había tenido trabajo Suzuki. Sin embargo, regresaron del descanso con bastante más energía y, cumplida la hora de partido, Okan Buruk llamó a Deniz Gül. Galatasaray ya tenía un '9' puro sobre el terreno de juego y, a menos de un cuarto de hora para el final del encuentro, se encontró un balón suelto a la salida de un córner que dio la victoria al conjunto turco. Se jugó el tipo el ex del Oporto porque, a la hora de meter la cabeza, Nico Jackson le propició una patada en la cara que le abrió la nariz. Desde luego, valió la pena... puesto que le dio al Galatasaray su tercera victoria consecutiva en esta Champions. Es, de hecho, la primera vez que lo logran a lo largo de sus participaciones en el torneo.

articles.title: Jamal Musiala: Bayern Munich hold talks over midfielder's health
articles.summary: Bayern Munich are only focused on getting Jamal Musiala back from injury and not interested in the comments made regarding his contract, the club's sporting director Max Eberl insists.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich are only focused on getting Jamal Musiala back from injury and are not interested in the comments made regarding his contract, the club's sporting director Max Eberl insisted.

The 23-year-old collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".

Last week, players' union Fifpro said Bayern Munich's hierarchy "should know better" after the club's honorary president Uli Hoeness said the midfielder may never "regain the performance level he once had".

Describing the talks on Tuesday as "very, very constructive", Eberl said the focus was on Musiala's recovery from a recent injury.

"Today it was about just how we want to get Jamal back on the field, just like before his muscle injury in the international break," Eberl said.

"That's the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something."

The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen questioned the lucrative contract extension the Germany international signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal , external may need to be renegotiated.

Bayern manager Vincent Kompany said in September it wouldn't be "a big deal" if the seizures return.

Musiala, previously a regular starter and one of the best young talents in Europe, has played five times this season, scoring twice.

"Contracts are there to be respected," Fifpro said on Saturday. "An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise."

articles.title: Cristiano continúa deshojando la margarita y Joao Félix presenta candidatura al Puskas
articles.standfirst: Ronaldo celebró, de penalti, su gol 987 y el ex del Atlético firmó una chilena descomunal
articles.summary: Ronaldo celebró, de penalti, su gol 987 y el ex del Atlético firmó una chilena descomunal
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo continúa deshojando la margarita en su objetivo por alcanzar los 1.000 goles en su carrera. A pesar de marcar en la derrota contra Al Ahli el pasado fin de semana en la Liga saudí, se fue con mal sabor de boca por fallar un penalti. Ante Al Sadd, en Champions asiática, se redimió arrancando el triunfo de un Al Nassr que Joao Félix se encargó de ratificar con una chilena digna de Puskas. No tardó Cristiano en poner por delante a Al Nassr firmando el gol 987 de su carrera. Después de calibrar mirilla con dos lanzamientos de falta, provocó un penalti antes de llegar al primer cuarto de hora tirando una elástica en el sector izquierdo del área que recordó a sus mejores tiempos. Agarró el balón, cruzó su disparo... y lo puso en la escuadra con una violencia tremenda. Se relajó Al Nassr y, menos de 10' después, Al Sadd logró volver a igualar el marcador. Akram Afif, el mejor jugador en la historia del fútbol qatarí, filtró un balón desde la frontal que Mohammed Waad resolvió ante un Bento que, escasos minutos después, tuvo que estirarse abajo para negarle el doblete. Debía reconectarse Al Nassr y, antes de poner rumbo al descanso, volvió a aparecer Cristiano para empujar un balón a placer a pase de Angelo. El asistente, sin embargo, levantó la bandera para anular el gol por fuera de juego en el origen de la acción. No lo tenía claro el portugués... pero parecía claro. Se quedó con un jugador menos Al Sadd en el descuento de la primera parte después de que el VAR atisbase que Mohammed Waad había escupido a Boushal. No fue el único contratiempo para el conjunto qatarí, que también perdió por lesión a Giovani superada la primera media hora. Se volcó Al Nassr desde que dio comienzo la segunda mitad. Se 'enchufó' Joao Félix y, en el 52', clavó una chilena atronadora desde, prácticamente, fuera del área. Entre club y selección, el 'menino' ya ha producido 22 goles en lo que marcha de temporada... mientras los rumores que le sitúan de vuelta en Europa no paran de crecer. Desde luego, lo está mereciendo.

articles.title: Amine Birouk, tras la decisión del TAS sobre la Copa África: "La vida sigue, pero hay que defender nuestros intereses"
articles.standfirst: El periodista de Radio MARS cuestiona el fallo del tribunal y apunta al Tribunal Federal Suizo como última vía de recurso.
articles.summary: El periodista de Radio MARS cuestiona el fallo del tribunal y apunta al Tribunal Federal Suizo como última vía de recurso.
articles.body: La polémica final de la Copa África entre Marruecos y Senegal ha sumado un nuevo capítulo. El Tribunal Arbitral del Deporte (TAS) ha revocado la decisión que había otorgado el título a Marruecos y ha devuelto el campeonato a Senegal, una resolución que ha provocado un profundo malestar en el país norteafricano. Para analizar las consecuencias de este fallo, Carlos Vicente Gómez ha entrevistado a Amine Birouk, periodista marroquí de Radio MARS, en el programa Otra Ronda de Radio MARCA. Durante la conversación, Birouk ha expresado su decepción por la resolución y ha cuestionado tanto los argumentos jurídicos del tribunal como la actuación de la Confederación Africana de Fútbol (CAF). El periodista ha explicado que en Marruecos existía cierto presentimiento de que la resolución no sería favorable. Según ha relatado, la prensa marroquí había informado de una supuesta comunicación telefónica, el pasado domingo, entre el árbitro del procedimiento Ulrich Haas y una de las partes implicadas, apenas 48 horas antes de conocerse el veredicto. Birouk considera que esta circunstancia merece atención y plantea dudas sobre el desarrollo del procedimiento arbitral. Uno de los principales argumentos de Birouk se centra en la interpretación que el tribunal ha hecho de los acontecimientos de la final. A su juicio, los jueces han dado prioridad al hecho de que el encuentro se reanudara, dejando en un segundo plano lo sucedido después de señalarse el penalti favorable a Marruecos. El periodista ha recordado que los jugadores de Senegal abandonaron el terreno de juego y que el partido permaneció interrumpido durante aproximadamente 22 minutos. También ha señalado los incidentes protagonizados por parte del público senegalés, con intentos de invasión del campo. Birouk sostiene que la decisión de Marruecos de continuar disputando el encuentro estuvo condicionada por el contexto institucional de aquella final, en la que se encontraban presentes, entre otras autoridades, el presidente de la FIFA y el de la Confederación Africana de Fútbol. El periodista marroquí también ha dirigido sus críticas hacia la CAF, a la que responsabiliza de no haber defendido adecuadamente su anterior resolución ante el TAS. La comisión de apelación de la confederación había dado inicialmente la razón a Marruecos, pero el tribunal deportivo ha terminado revocando aquella decisión. Birouk ha cuestionado la capacidad jurídica del organismo africano y ha recordado que, según sus datos, de siete procedimientos en los que la CAF ha comparecido ante el TAS, ha perdido seis. En su opinión, este desenlace perjudica la credibilidad de la institución y deja en entredicho el valor de sus decisiones jurídicas. La Federación Marroquí de Fútbol ya ha manifestado públicamente su desacuerdo con el fallo y ha anunciado su intención de defender sus intereses hasta la última instancia. Entre los argumentos expuestos figura la supuesta comunicación del árbitro Ulrich Haas y la falta de consideración de determinadas decisiones anteriores de los organismos futbolísticos. La última posibilidad pasaría por acudir al Tribunal Federal Suizo. Sin embargo, Birouk ha reconocido que las opciones son reducidas: según ha explicado, este órgano únicamente admite una pequeña proporción de los recursos y su intervención requiere denunciar defectos de forma en el procedimiento. Pese al malestar, el periodista ha querido lanzar un mensaje de perspectiva y ha defendido que Marruecos no debe convertir este episodio en una obsesión. Birouk ha insistido en que la derrota institucional no debe eclipsar el crecimiento del fútbol marroquí durante los últimos años. Ha destacado los éxitos de sus selecciones, como el Mundial sub-20, la histórica semifinal mundialista de 2022, los resultados posteriores en las grandes competiciones y el impulso al fútbol femenino. Además, ha puesto el foco en el futuro, especialmente en el Mundial de 2030, que Marruecos organizará junto a España y Portugal, y en la preparación de las próximas competiciones continentales. "La vida sigue", ha resumido el periodista, que considera necesario defender los intereses del fútbol marroquí sin perder de vista los objetivos deportivos e institucionales del país. Birouk también ha asegurado que la polémica puede marcar un antes y un después en el fútbol, al considerar que el comportamiento de Senegal durante aquella final ha contribuido a cambiar la interpretación de las normas sobre el abandono del terreno de juego. Por el momento, Marruecos espera acontecimientos y no descarta continuar la batalla jurídica. Mientras tanto, Senegal vuelve a figurar como campeón de África en una de las finales más controvertidas que se recuerdan en el fútbol continental.

articles.title: Leaked FIFA Documents Show Infantino's 96-Year Private Equity Plan for World Cup
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Gianni Infantino 's failed private equity plan that provoked the biggest crisis of his FIFA presidency intended to sell stakes in the World Cup for 96 years.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Gianni Infantino 's failed private equity plan that provoked the biggest crisis of his FIFA presidency intended to sell stakes in the World Cup for 96 years.

Documents exchanged between FIFA and investor Joshua Kushner's firm Thrive Capital, reviewed Tuesday by The Associated Press, also show the planned $20 billion FIFA Forward Enterprises subsidiary could have paid tens of millions of dollars in management bonuses to its executives.

The leaked documents, first reported Monday by the New York Post, show how the FFE deal was moving toward completion in New York on the weekend of the July 19 final of the men's World Cup.

The secretive project was revealed nine days after the final by British daily The Times and the global backlash, including from senior FIFA executives, pushed Infantino to withdraw the proposal within days.

The leaked documents, including a FIFA in-house risk assessment, show its own finance officials "were not directly privy to the construction of this transaction."

"This deal provides for Fifa to create a for-profit subsidiary which would have all the commercial rights for FIFA events transferred to it for commercial exploitation for the next 96 years," the risk assessment states.

Infantino now faces a first presidential election challenge since he was elected in 2016, with two opponents campaigning ahead of a March 18 vote in Morocco: Philippe Diallo of France and Kohzo Tashima of Japan.

The FFE private equity plan reignited concerns in Europe and Japan about Infantino's leadership style and political ties to U.S. President Donald Trump, over creating a FIFA peace prize and waiving a mandatory one-game ban at the World Cup for United States forward Folarin Balogun.

The leaked documents show FIFA was in talks with the Affinity Partners investment firm of Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, before settling on his younger brother Joshua's firm Thrive Capital as anchor investor.

Affinity Partners was cited in one document which explained why FIFA did not open a tender process "owing to the specific and unique nature of the proposed investment, bilateral and unilateral conversations held with interest from several potential investment sources."

Thrive created a "Backstop Letter and Transaction Terms" document dated July 17 about the plan with FIFA called "Project Box."

The document detailed a "Management Incentive Plan" with bonuses to be decided by the FFE board chaired by the sitting president, Infantino.

"This is customary for proposed structures of this nature," FIFA said in a statement about the project which it had repeatedly said was a proposal needing to be approved by its 211 member federations. They effectively own FIFA as a Switzerland-based non-profit.

"FIFA's leadership would only have had leading roles in the board, which would not have led to any additional remuneration," the world soccer body said.

articles.title: Jersey Mike's Trophy: Oxford United draw with Tottenham Under-21s to progress
articles.summary: Aaron Ramsey's Oxford United beat Tottenham Under-21s to secure one of the final two Jersey Mike's Trophy knockout spots.
articles.body:
Aaron Ramsey's Oxford United beat Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1 to secure one of the final two Jersey Mike's Trophy knockout spots.

Oxford knew avoiding defeat by a margin of four goals or more would be enough to seal progression from Southern Group A alongside already-qualified Exeter City.

They trailed to Tyler Tingey's early opener on Tuesday, which gave Spurs' youngsters a glimmer of hope of pulling off that mini-miracle.

But Jun'ai Byfield's own goal and 18-year-old Jack Lee's late winner ensured ex-Arsenal man Ramsey got one over his old north London rivals as Oxford won to finish top of the group.

Elsewhere, Fleetwood's decisive Northern Group G match at home to Leeds United Under-21s was put back 24 hours because of a waterlogged pitch.

The two sides will now meet on Wednesday to decide who progresses alongside group leaders Oldham Athletic to complete the line-up for the knockout stages.

There were wins for League Two pair Tranmere Rovers and Salford City over Premier League sides in Tuesday's other two ties, which were virtually dead rubbers.

Tranmere, who had already sealed their last-32 spot, came from behind to beat eliminated Everton Under-21s 2-1 with goals from David Kamara and Charlie Veevers in Northern Group E.

Both Salford City and Sunderland Under-21s had already been eliminated from Northern Group A but goals from Paolo Mariani, Brandon Cooper and Kyrell Malcolm gave the Ammies a 3-2 win despite Jaydon Jones' Black Cats double.

Of the 16 Premier League under-21 sides to enter the competition, with one placed in each group, only six have progressed to the knockout rounds, although Leeds can still make that number seven.

The last-32 draw will take place on Wednesday at 16:30 GMT. Ties will take place in the week commencing 7 December.

All 16 group winners are guaranteed a home tie, with fixtures remaining regionalised until the semi-final stage.

articles.standfirst: Te contamos todos los detalles para que no te pierdas nada de la quinta jornada
articles.summary: Te contamos todos los detalles para que no te pierdas la quinta jornada de la competición
articles.body: El Sabah y el Barcelona se enfrentan en el partido correspondiente a la jornada 5 de la liguilla de la Champions League. El encuentro se disputa este miércoles 25 de noviembre a las 18.45 horas en el Estadio Olímpico de Bakú, en Azerbaiyán. El cruce está marcado por los muchos kilómetros que recorrerá el cuadro catalán. El bloque culé tuvo que viajar el lunes al mediodía. Los azulgranas llegan al partido tras remontar el domingo el cruce contra el Villarreal en el Spotify Camp Nou que se les puso muy cuesta arriba, con un 0-2 en los primeros compases. El partido entre el Sabah y Barcelona se disputa el miércoles 25 de noviembre a las 18.45 horas. El partido entre el Sabah y el Barcelona de la jornada 5 de la Champions League se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través de Movistar Liga de Campeones. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles. El Sabah llega al encuentro contra el Barcelona en la parte más baja de la tabla. Ocupa la posición 31 de la clasificación y solo ha logrado un triunfo en los primeros cinco encuentros, tras ganar al Slavia de Praga. El Barcelona llega al encuentro contra el Sabah en la quinta posición de la tabla y tras ganar su último partido, por 3-0, contra el Aston Villa.
