articles.title: Cardiff City 0-4 Preston North End: Graham Alexander's side romp to victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Cardiff City and Preston North End at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday night; Lilywhites off bottom with emphatic victory after the Bluebirds who were previously unbeaten at home this season.
articles.body:
It was their first win on the road this season and made it seven points from their last three games after a win over Southampton and a draw at West Ham.

Thierry Small scored in the 25th minute, Alfie Devine fired home in the 33rd, Andy Moran joined them on the scoresheet in the 62nd and then skipper Andrew Hughes headed home in the 69th.

It was a tactical masterclass from Alexander's men as they completely nullified Cardiff's usual free-flowing approach and forced the home side into error after error.

It took a brilliant piece of defending from Liam Lindsay to deny top scorer Jack Moylan a tap into an empty net in the fourth minute, but after that the Preston goal was not threatened until the end of the first half.

Moran forced Nathan Trott to punch his dipping shot clear before Preston opened the scoring with a back-post finish from Small as he converted a low cross from the right by Stan Mills.

Six minutes later and Cardiff were punished again for giving away the ball. Moran stole the ball from Ronan Kpakio 30 yards out and drove to the edge of the area before picking out Devine, who stroked the ball into the bottom left corner passed a helpless Trott.

Cardiff fired off a few shots in the dying embers of the half, one of which from Ollie Tanner had to be dealt with, but it had been the worst 45 minutes of football by the Bluebirds at home this season.

Not much changed in the second period as Preston continued to prove the sharper and better-connected team. Devine earned a corner in the opening minute with a shot that took a deflection before Tanner and Rubin Colwill shot wide of the posts for the home side.

An attempted pass to Cardiff skipper Colwill some 30 yards out from his goal by substitute Chris Willock missed its target and gave Moran the chance to pick up the pieces, carry up to the edge of the area before unleashing a shot that went over Trott after catching the boot of defender Joel Bagan.

As if that was not bad enough for the Cardiff fans, who are preparing for one of their biggest games of the season on Sunday against arch-rivals Swansea, they saw their side concede a fourth in the 69th minute when Hughes rose above Colwill to head home from a corner.

"We thought we could produce a good performance and win but it wasn't possible. We gave the ball away too often and that gave them clear chances on our goal and they took them.

"We have to own the result and own that performance. We have to wake up tomorrow and concentrate on what's going to be a great game on Sunday.

"We didn't play well and we have to accept that. We have to be miles better to win games and we have shown we can do that against the best teams in the division.

"We need to play better. Our game is based on a high technical level and when we build up at the back, it's with a really clear idea to progress really quickly to the opponent's last line in a really aggressive manner."

"I'm ecstatic, it was a brilliant performance. I'm so pleased for the players and the supporters that came down on a Tuesday night all this way to see us.

"The players were magnificent tonight. I think the way they've approached the last two games especially, against massive clubs at this level, and then coming to this place to face an undefeated side was great.

"Cardiff had scored a lot of goals and they're a really good team. So to keep a clean sheet, and to score four goals, shows it was a really clinical and a super professional performance.

"Every player had a role to play for his team-mates and for the collective, and they did it well. They were magnificent, and the subs that came on impacted the game as well.

"Hopefully they'll keep gaining confidence, keep believing in themselves because they are good players. Hopefully the clarity we're trying to create for them will help them.

"It took a few weeks for me to understand what the challenge was and what they've been through, but they're showing great signs of becoming the team that we believe they can be."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Charlton Athletic 4-0 Lincoln City: Addicks sweep to victory at The Valley
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Charlton Athletic and Lincoln City at The Valley on Tuesday night; Addicks secure their most emphatic win of the season so far as they thump four past Imps.
articles.body:
Joe Rankin-Costello's first goal of the season quickly broke the deadlock with Ivan Mesik doubling the Addicks' advantage inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Tyreece Campbell's finish early in the second half ended any lingering doubts that the Imps were heading for a fifth straight Championship loss.

Miles Leaburn's stoppage-time goal was nothing less than the utterly dominant home team deserved.

Charlton moved up to 15th in the standings after easily their most fluid performance of the season to make it back-to-back wins on home soil.

The Addicks were rewarded for a fast start as they took the lead in the eighth minute. Rankin-Costello showed clinical composure to strike first time with a right-footed volley after Karlan Grant's cross was headed into his path by Tyler Bindon.

Some of the hosts early play was very slick and they made it 2-0 after 13 minutes through Mesik. The Slovakian international converted at the back post from Campbell's cross from the right side of the penalty box.

Lincoln would have been facing a far heavier deficit by the interval if goalkeeper George Wickens had not made a number of vital saves.

The Imps number one twice pushed over full-blooded attempts by Grant and also denied Matty Godden in the 34th minute as the rampant home side looked to add to their haul.

Wickham made one more stop on the stroke of half-time to swat away Conor Coventry's looping shot which threatened to dip in.

Lincoln failed to have a shot in the first period but their bench was aggrieved that an early tackle in the box by Bindon on Mikkel Ladefoged was not penalised by referee Oliver Langford.

The Imps made a triple change at the start of the second half but quickly fell further behind. Campbell was in the right place to drive the ball home - his sixth goal of the campaign - after Wickens could only parry Godden's shot in the 48th minute.

It continued to be one-way attacking traffic in favour of the Addicks and Wickens turned Grant's deflected strike around his left post.

Coventry was guilty of a glaring miss after being gifted the ball by Ben House in the 81st minute. The Republic of Ireland international had the goal at his mercy but was unable to hit the target from 16 yards.

Campbell kicked the advertising board after Wickens denied him a second goal from a tight angle, the Jamaican international showing electric pace to latch on to Coventry's long pass.

Leaburn added the fourth, pouncing from close range from fellow substitute Josh Edwards' low cross.

"That is probably the best performance since I've been at the football club. I know we have won games here by big margins but that was in League One. We went away to Ipswich and won 3-0 but that was the most complete performance.

"We started really well and should've scored before we did. But when we got the goal we went on. Their keeper was outstanding. We had 33 shots tonight and 13 on target.

"I'm not disappointed with 4-0 because I would've taken it all day but we've had some clear-cut chances tonight which we haven't taken.

"It is a wonderful night. The way we passed the ball, the penetration we had and the chances created, we were excellent.

"We use the word relentless at our football club quite a lot and we demonstrated that tonight.

"Today there was a lot of pressure. It was a must-win game, considering where we were and Lincoln were. The players showed a quality and confidence that defies any negativity anywhere."

"There wasn't anything to be proud of tonight and I can only apologise to the supporters that have travelled and make sure that doesn't happen again. It can't happen again - we can't play like that against any team in the Championship, let alone Wolves on Saturday afternoon.

"We weren't good enough from the first minute to the last, we didn't do the basics well enough. We will go away and assess everything tactical and technical.

"We didn't give ourselves a chance because five minutes into the game it felt like everything they did was positive and we didn't connect passes or take the positive action, which we do whenever we play well.

"We had a little bit of illness in the camp in terms of the team that would have been playing instead of the team that started the game which wasn't ideal, but there is no way we're using that as an excuse. The team was good enough to come to Charlton and put in a better account than what we did."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Wolverhampton Wanderers 3-0 Derby County: Adam Armstrong nets twice in Wolves win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Derby County at Molineux on Tuesday night; Adam Armstrong scores twice as Wolves sweep to victory past the Rams.
articles.body:
Armstrong's double sandwiched Mateus Mane's first of the season as Wolves' fourth straight win stretched their unbeaten run to eight games to climb a place to second in the table.

And despite a couple of first-half scares from Derby, Wolves could have had several more goals, while Derby are now bottom after one win in 13.

Clean-through Carlton Morris had the chance to give Derby a surprise second-minute lead, but Nasser Djiga made a vital tackle.

Wolves soon started creating chances as Derby sat back.

Ladislav Krejci glanced wide from a corner before Hugo Bueno's 25-yard angled drive was deflected wide.

Mane and Fer Lopez both then side-footed straight at Derby goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterstrom.

A cross missed by Krejci gave Derby's Filip Bilbija a sniff of goal but Krejci desperately hacked clear before the winger could shoot, Mohammed Fuseini lobbing over the loose ball.

Wolves returned to the attack where Andre lifted a rising effort comfortably over the bar.

Derby breached Wolves' back line again only to hit the woodwork.

Widell Zetterstrom's free-kick was won by Matt Clarke and Morris' shot hit Krejci before Fuseini crashed a shot against Jose Sa's head then against the outside of the bar.

Wolves responded by taking a 29th-minute lead through Armstrong.

Mane did brilliantly to shake off Clarke on the touchline before pulling it back for Tommy Doyle, whose shot was blocked, Armstrong tucking away the loose ball.

Armstrong was inches away when he stabbed wide from Bueno's diagonal pass.

Rafiki Said missed two chances to have doubled Wolves' lead just after half-time.

He headed over unmarked from Kieran Trippier's cross. Then he took the ball too close to Widell Zetterstrom in a one-on-one.

Wolves continued to threaten and Djiga headed powerfully over from Trippier's corner before Doyle's deflected chip sailed just wide.

An inviting cross from Mane was missed by Widell Zetterstrom but hit Said's thigh with the goal at his mercy, before Lopez and then Armstrong fired just wide.

Despite their dominance, Wolves had not forced a serious save from Widell Zetterstrom until he palmed Bueno's rising shot upwards.

Wolves finally got their long overdue second goal in the 74th minute.

Substitute Rodrigo Gomes drove in a fierce low cross and Mane gleefully steered home.

Armstrong made it 3-0 two minutes later, volleying into the far corner from just inside the box, though Widell Zetterstrom got a hand to it.

"It was a perfect night. We deserved the win and could have scored more goals but it was a great team performance.

"In the first few minutes they created two or three situations because we didn't have the right balance.

"But we deserved the win because the players were enjoying the game and we wanted to win for the fans. The lads did a great job.

"I spoke to the players because we know our opponents stay in a low block on the edge of the box and sometimes that's difficult, so we have to shoot more from outside the box.

"In the second half the space opened up a bit more to allow us to create more chances."

"I was happy with the first-half performance apart from the last five or six minutes.

"We had two or three chances which we didn't take and against a top team you can't afford to let them off.

"Then we tired in the second half and we didn't come out at all really.

"We looked leggy and we continued in that rhythm. But that will improve with Matt Clarke, Shane Duffy and Jack Robinson coming back.

"I said to the lads you can't feel sorry for yourselves. We had a really solid performance against Southampton but when you come to a place like this, you can't afford to not do the hard work and take a break."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Portsmouth 1-0 West Ham United: Scott Parker stays winless as Odin Bailey nets Pompey winner
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Portsmouth and West Ham United at Fratton Park on Tuesday night; Odin Bailey scores the only goal as Pompey beat Hammers to leave Scott Parker without a win.
articles.body:
Parker has lost two and drawn two since replacing Nuno Espirito Santo in the Hammers dugout, with the east Londoners without victory in six and 11 points off the top of the table.

The Championship's top scorers West Ham failed to scored for the first time this season, despite hitting the woodwork twice, as Bailey's first-half strike was enough for Portsmouth to rise to 10th.

Academy graduate goalkeeper Finlay Herrick was drafted into the Hammers starting XI at the weekend in place of Mads Hermansen, but the 20-year-old had a first half to forget after keeping his spot in the team.

He got away with flapping at Bailey's fourth-minute corner as Ebou Adams scooped the ball over the bar from close range.

But Herrick was punished for a weak punch at Tyrese Shade's dangerous cross from the right in the 31st minute and his poor connection went straight to Bailey, who thumped his finish under the keeper.

Bailey's first goal since arriving from Stockport was a bad omen for the Hammers, who had failed to win on the previous nine matches they had conceded first this season.

There had been a general air of nervousness about the visitors - without a win since October 17 - but they still created strong openings.

Jarrod Bowen showed pace on the right before his shot was pushed on to a post by Nicolas Schmid in the early stages.

Portsmouth goalkeeper Schmid has come under scrutiny of his own and did well to deny Joel Piroe twice but also had his own punching gaffe.

The Austrian managed to punch Arne Engles' corner behind him, but Madiodio Dia spared his blushes on the line as Mohamadou Kante lurked for a tap-in.

The Hammers had a claim for a penalty at the start of the second half when Konstantinos Mavropanos flung himself to the ground under Adams' tackle, but Andrew Kitchen waved the shouts away.

Engels struck a free-kick into Schmid's midriff before the Belgian was set up with a golden headed chance by Edvin Austbo, but his effort flew over the arriving Tomas Soucek and wide.

The hosts still offered a threat and almost doubled their lead in extraordinary style when Abu Kamara volleyed a raking through-ball wide.

It seemed to add a desperation to West Ham's attacking as Austbo headed at Schmid before the keeper produced a showstopping save to push Soucek's rasping shot on to the crossbar, but they could find an equaliser.

"I'm really pleased for Odin. One thing we recruited him for was his goals and assists for Stockport.

"If we can translate that League One form into the Championship then we'll be happy.

"He has a very good left foot and contributions with goals and assists will hopefully start to come for him.

"He has had a tough start to his Portsmouth career and had to bide his time. He's come in now and taken his chance.

"I thought we were superb. You take any win against West Ham. You know it is going to be hard-earned.

"The nature of the win as well, we properly deserved it in the first half and then dug in in the second."

"It was a little bit groundhog - we had our chances today, but my overall feeling is that it is close but so far.

"I have not been in here long, but those are the feelings I have and we need to address that. The reality is the reality in this moment in time.

"They scored with their first attack and that has given us a mountain to climb. We had our chances and hit the woodwork, but I can't say that we were unlucky.

"You earn your luck and we aren't doing it.

"This league is up and down, but my main focus at the moment is this team and there are more important things to address - ie we are too easy to score against which gives us a lot to do.

"I knew it was a tough job when I arrived and knew it would be tough for anyone. The pressure is immense when you come out of the Premier League and the numbers (to get promoted) are against you.

"There is quality here, but you need more than quality in this league."

articles.title: Hibernian 2-1 Dundee: Goals from Martin Boyle and Chris Cadden secure Hibs' win at Easter Road for first time in eight months
articles.summary: Report as Hibernian win at Easter Road for the first time this season; Martin Boyle opened the scoring from the penalty spot; Nicky Cadden added a second; Joe Wright pulled a goal back for Dundee; Hibs move up to ninth in the Scottish Premiership; Dundee remain seventh
articles.body:
Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden - who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box - had the hosts in command before the interval.

But Dundee showed plenty of fight after the break and pulled one back through Joe Wright.

The visitors tried in vain to grab an equaliser and it was Hibs who were left satisfied by their first three points at home since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Despite being thrashed by Dundee United 4-0 at the weekend, Hibernian head coach Marink Reedijk decided to make only two alterations to his team, with Cadden and Thibault Klidje coming in.

Dundee manager Steven Pressley changed half of his outfield XI following the 8-0 humiliation to Hearts.

Owen Bevan was suspended and in came on-loan Bournemouth defender Matai Akinmboni for a full debut while Joe Wright, Brad Halliday, Joe Bevan and Ashley Hay started.

Hibs played on the front foot as they looked to start repairing the damage from the weekend's demoralising loss.

On a rare start, Togo international Klidje was lively and saw a header crash into the side-netting before hitting a harmless snap-shot straight at Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

From a short corner routine Hibs worked space for Cadden on the edge of the box from Josh Mulligan's lay-off and his driving effort whistled just past a post.

Dundee were desperate to keep it tight at the back but offered little going forward. Just when it looked like they were beginning to settle Hibs hit them two goals in three minutes before the break.

The first came in the 40th minute when Boyle fired a penalty past Goodman after being tripped by Ryan Finnigan.

Cadden then found the top corner with a sublime curling effort from his left foot just outside the box. It was another short corner routine that saw Miguel Chaiwa set up the wing-back.

Despite the hammer blow of losing two goals in quick succession before the break, Dundee demonstrated at the start of the second half that they were not going to roll over.

Pressley's side upped their intensity as they searched for a goal to get themselves back in the game and that arrived in the 67th minute courtesy of Wright.

Substitute Callum Jones' free-kick should have been put away by Ryan Astley but the ball broke back to Wright and he slammed the ball high into the net from six yards.

That set up a tense finish but Hibs desperately held on for a rare home victory.

"It's always nice to win, it's a good one again in order to make sure we get confirmation that if we show our identity about intensity, aggression and proactivity and are brave, that anything can happen here.

"I hope we get another three points next match and that we go again in a way that we do the things we are good at and what our identity and what we stand for is.

"The next match against Motherwell is not at home, I know, but there will be a match at home against Rangers, where this can also come to life again. But that is far away.

"First things first, Saturday lies another challenge."

"Both teams are a bit fragile and there was a lot of trepidation in the game but the one thing about us we got a degree of pride back. It's not the result but a little bit of stability and we showed a lot of courage.

"We wanted to give ourselves a foundation to build from and we gave ourselves that.

"We were much more cohesive in the second half and when you suffer the defeat we suffered on Saturday and you come here and you find yourself 2-0 down at half-time, it asks a lot of questions of you as a group and I thought they responded brilliantly.

"They showed courage and spirit and it's not been easy because there's a fragility about us. We responded in the proper manner."

articles.title: Norwich City 1-1 Queens Park Rangers: Anthony Musaba earns a point for the Canaries
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Norwich City and Queens Park Rangers at Carrow Road on Tuesday night; Canaries draw their first game of the season as Anthony Musaba cancels out Harvey Vale’s opener.
articles.body:
The Canaries had won their previous five Championship fixtures but had to come from behind to pick up a point this time around after Harvey Vale had fired the visitors in front just before the break.

Philippe Clement's side were quickly back on level terms in the second half through a well-taken Anthony Musaba effort, but were well contained after that as Rangers registered a well-deserved point.

After a slow start, the match burst into life with a flurry of activity around the mid-point of the first half.

Norwich thought they had taken the lead on 19 minutes when Harry Darling got a touch on an in-swinging Jacob Wright free-kick but the effort was ruled out for offside.

Andre Brooks then saw a low shot from the edge of the area come back off the upright, while at the other end Dan Grimshaw did well to palm away a goal-bound effort from Vale.

Rangers were giving the hosts plenty to think about and took the lead four minutes before the break when Vale made another opportunity count.

The Republic of Ireland international had plenty to do after latching on to Kealey Adamson's pass but despite having Ruairi McConville and Darling in close attendance, he worked himself some space in the area before firing a powerful shot past Grimshaw.

Norwich were back on level terms within three minutes of the restart after a poor clearance by goalkeeper Pierce Charles was punished. It went straight to Musaba, who played a quick one-two with Mathias Kvistgaarden before confidently finding the roof of the net.

Vale fired inches wide as Rangers sought a quick response while substitute Oscar Schwartau was foiled by a good save from Charles as the game entered its final 10 minutes.

Norwich continued to press for a winner but could find no way through as they drew a game for the first time this season.

"This team will never settle for a draw - they will always keep going for the win but in football it doesn't always happen.

"After going behind we showed the right mentality, got our goal and kept pushing them back, with the fans playing their part, but unfortunately we couldn't get the second goal we deserved.

"We were up against a well-organised side and knew it was going to be tough but I thought the momentum was with us in the first half too and we just needed a bit of luck.

"We had a goal ruled out through a very tight offside decision and then Andre (Brooks) hit the post.

"When we went behind it became an even tougher task because we know how difficult they are to break down but our response was really good with everyone playing their part, including the lads who came off the bench."

"That's four points from two very tough away games, Millwall and Norwich, which is a very positive outcome and all credit to the players for that.

"We were up against a side who had won their previous five games, scoring 17 goals, and it was a very good performance, with a draw a fair result I feel.

"We started very well, both with and without the ball, playing with a good tempo, and scored a very good goal.

"Obviously we were disappointed to concede so early in the second half but the lads showed great character to stick to the game plan. They defended properly as a team and we also had some chances.

"I am lucky to have a special group of players here and although they are a young group I thought they showed great maturity out there to come away with a deserved point."

articles.title: La sentencia de Radio MARCA sobre Bellingham tras su golazo ante el PSV: "Es el mejor del mundo"
articles.standfirst: El inglés lideró la reacción del Real Madrid ante los neerlandeses
articles.summary: El inglés lideró la reacción del Real Madrid ante los neerlandeses
articles.body: Jude Bellingham volvió a reivindicar su condición de futbolista diferencial en el Madrid. El inglés fue uno de los grandes protagonistas de la remontada ante el PSV, con un golazo desde fuera del área que desató la admiración de los tertulianos del Marcador de Radio MARCA. Un tanto que no solo puso por delante a los blancos, sino que también reabrió el debate sobre el lugar que ocupa el centrocampista entre los mejores jugadores del mundo. El Real Madrid cambió por completo tras el descanso. Los ajustes de Mourinho, con las entradas de Konaté, Huijsen y Bellingham por Rüdiger, Militao y Tchouaméni, transformaron a un equipo que había sufrido durante la primera mitad. Fede Valverde igualó el encuentro en el minuto 50 y, diez minutos después, llegó el momento de Bellingham. El inglés recibió fuera del área y conectó un disparo potente y preciso que dejó sin opciones a Kovar. Una acción de enorme calidad que recordó a los grandes goles de su carrera y que no pasó inadvertida en la retransmisión de Radio MARCA. Javier Tintó fue contundente al valorar el tanto: «Me atrevería a decir que es el mejor gol de Jude desde que llegó al Madrid». El tertuliano fue más allá y defendió que Bellingham lleva tiempo siendo el mejor futbolista del planeta: «Lo vengo diciendo desde hace tiempo, que desde el Mundial es el mejor jugador del mundo. Este gol me recuerda a Zidane». Jaime Sánchez, exfutbolista y también tertuliano del Marcador, se sumó a los elogios con una valoración que define el perfil del inglés: «Es el mejor todocampista del mundo». La exhibición de Bellingham llegó en el momento que más necesitaba el Real Madrid. Después de una primera mitad llena de dudas, el inglés volvió a aparecer para cambiar el rumbo del encuentro y demostrar que su influencia va mucho más allá de los goles. Tras una primera mitad para el olvido, el marcador final fue 5-1 a favor de los merengues.

articles.title: El Betis se lo puede creer
articles.standfirst: Alcanza los doce puntos en Bratislava con un doblete del Cucho Hernández y acaricia el pase
articles.summary: Alcanza los doce puntos en Bratislava con un doblete del Cucho Hernández y acaricia el pase
articles.body: Era lo que marcaba el guión, pero a veces la puesta en escena falla y nada está garantizado. El Betis rascó en su visita al peor equipo de esta Champions League. En Bratislava, los de Pellegrini firmaron un triunfo de oficio, de esos que garantizan los típicos equipos de fuerte jerarquía en la competición. Ganó el Betis al Slovan, volvió a marcar el Cucho Hernández, por partida doble, y el equipo verdiblanco, con doce puntos apilados en su brillante trayectoria, ya ve con claridad en el horizonte la siguiente fase. Se puede soñar. Se debe soñar. Ahí está el Betis, con 12 de 15 puntos posibles en la parte noble de la clasificación. Queda un calendario terrorífico, pero el colchón es mullido. Lo suficiente para sentirse cómodo en esta Champions League. Son los de Pellegrini un equipo hecho, fiable, y con ese punto de mordiente arriba que es capaz de darle un susto casi a cualquiera. El Betis puede ser la revelación de esta edición. Ha sentado las bases para ello. Y eso que el Slovan, con cinco derrotas ya en los mismos partidos y un global de un gol a favor y 18 en contra -se dice pronto- no fue, en apariencia, ese rival tan asequible. Salieron valientes los de Touré, generaron situaciones de ventaja en el último tercio de campo y se defendieron relativamente bien, salvo en contados desajustes. Le faltaron muchas cosas, obviamente, pero su partido no es el de un equipo desahuciado en cuanto a resultados. O al menos así fue durante 45 minutos. En un primer tiempo bastante equilibrado, de hecho, la primera gran ocasión fue para los de Touré. Se quedó en el mano a mano Sporar con un Valles que achicó con rapidez. Otro cara a cara también lo mandó al limbo Abde al encontrarse con una mano milagrosa de Takac. Eso sería ya en una fase en la que los de Pellegrini comenzaron a mostrar su superioridad. En ese tramo final del primer tiempo llegó el gol del Cucho. De puro nueve. Un centro medido al segundo palo de Ortiz lo cabeceó el colombiano elevándose por encima de todos. No es el más alto, pero sí el más intenso y el más listo de los que transitaban por el verde de Bratislava. Solo así se explica que repitiese maniobra a la salida de vestuarios. Ahí, en esa segunda mitad, se vio el Slovan colista, el que va de goleada en goleada. El Betis se frotó las manos con la facilidad que encontraba a la hora de atacar los espacios. Pero fue a balón parado, desde la esquina, donde el Cucho volvió a suspenderse en el aire para cabecear a la red. Dos testarazos de nota. La última media hora fue un monólogo verdiblanco. Un rival entregado, un Betis de control y la sensación de que si eso no terminaba en goleada es porque los de Pellegrini no querían emplearse a fondo. Tan claro lo vio el chileno que dio descanso a Isco y el Cucho con mucho partido todavía por delante. El final fue un paseo. Un homenaje a esta primera fase en la que el Betis firma un camino casi impoluto. Quién lo hubiera dicho. Camino de la historia. Sin complejos y con mucho fútbol. Como para no creer.

articles.title: Guardiola ya se hace extrañar en el Manchester City
articles.standfirst: Cherki acabó rescatando un empate ante un Nápoles que se puso por delante hasta en dos ocasiones
articles.summary: Cherki acabó rescatando un empate ante un Nápoles que se puso por delante hasta en dos ocasiones
articles.body: Nadie dijo que fuese a ser fácil... y el Manchester City ya está empezando a extrañar a Pep Guardiola. Suman cuatro jornadas consecutivas sin ganar en Premier y, con el duelo ante el Arsenal en el horizonte más próximo, el empate en Champions contra un Nápoles en horas bajas deja en una posición muy delicada a Enzo Maresca. La dinámica reciente del equipo obligaba a Maresca a tomar decisiones y realizó hasta cinco cambios respecto al once que empató ante el Fulham. Sorprendió la titularidad de Allan en banda izquierda, mientras que Anderson, Bouaddi y Enzo compartieron sala de máquinas. Todos los focos, sin embargo, se los llevó De Bruyne en su retorno al Etihad con la camiseta del Nápoles. El City se adueñó de la posesión desde que el balón se puso en marcha y, ante la pasividad de los hombres de Allegri, se instaló en campo rival. Elliot Anderson tanteó a Milinkovic-Savic en los primeros compases. A partir de entonces, sin embargo, comenzaron a hacerse presentes los problemas a la hora de darle ritmo a sus circulaciones que vienen lastrando al conjunto 'cityzen'. A pesar de estar extremadamente hundido, no se sentía incómodo el Nápoles. Mathías Olivera, eso sí, se jugó un penalti rondando el 20' intentando cerrar un centro en dirección a Haaland en el segundo palo. Fue lo más cerca que estuvo del gol en toda la primera parte. Estuvo completamente desabastecido y no llegó a conectar ni un remate. El Nápoles, extremadamente comprometido y solidario, fue reforzando su planteamiento con el paso de los minutos. Apenas estaban pudiendo expandirse. Beukema, sin embargo, se apuntó la ocasión más clara del choque. Tuvo que exprimirse Donnarumma para repeler el 'cabezazo' del neerlandés a la salida de un córner. Calentaron varios miembros del banquillo 'cityzen' durante el descanso... pero Maresca no consideró que fuese necesario intervenir tan pronto. Sin embargo, el tanto de Hojlund en el 55' dejó helado al Etihad. En una de las pocas acciones en las que el Nápoles se animó a lanzar la presión, lograron recuperar alto, Gilmour filtró sobre el danés y éste se habilitó el espacio para batir a Donnarumma. Reaccionó Maresca de inmediato renovando los extremos con Doku y Ndiaye. Se fue Allan, que apenas tuvo incidencia en el choque, y un Enzo Fernández que volvió a firmar una actuación tremendamente gris. El belga, en una de sus primeras acciones, aprovechó una desconexión del Nápoles en un balón parado para asistir a un Ayyoub Bouaddi que se estrenó como 'sky blue'. El gol renovó energías en un Manchester City que tenía más de 20' para intentar darle la vuelta al encuentro. Se lanzaron a por la remontada... y abrieron la puerta para que el Nápoles volviese a ponerse por delante. Estiró Spinazzola por derecha y sirvió un centro al segundo palo que Noa Lang empalmó de primeras. Milinkovic-Savic realizó varias intervenciones de mérito para intentar conservar la victoria del Nápoles. A menos de cinco minutos para que se cumpliese el tiempo reglamentario, sin embargo, Cherki frotó la lámpara para, al menos, rescatar un punto en favor del City. Se coló en el área y definió con un disparo raso, cruzado y ajustado al poste. De lo poco salvable.

articles.title: Bellingham resucita al Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: El inglés, suplente, sale en el descanso con 0-1 para convertir a un equipo muerto ante el PSV en el viejo Rey de Europa. Vinicius se libera al cerrar la goleada y provoca el abrazo del grupo
articles.summary: El inglés, suplente, sale en el descanso con 0-1 para convertir a un equipo muerto ante el PSV en el viejo Rey de Europa. Vinicius se libera al cerrar la goleada y provoca el abrazo del grupo
articles.body: Jude Bellingham. No busquen más. El fútbol del inglés, con el 5 a la espalda que inmortalizó Zidane, es capaz de resucitar a un muerto, que es lo que parecía el Real Madrid al descanso. El equipo blanco se fue al descanso por debajo en el marcador y zarandeado en el juego por un asombroso PSV, presionante a todo campo. Pero corrigió Mourinho, metió a Zinedine Bellingham junto a los centrales titulares y arrasó al equipo neerlandés. Goleó en medio partido por fútbol, por actitud y por acierto, redimiendo a quienes acababan de recibir pitos. Como Mbappé, autor de un doblete. Y también, por fin, como Vinicius, que cerró la goleada con un buen tanto y el abrazo colectivo de un equipo en racha. Cinco de cinco. Pie y medio en octavos. Pese al buen sabor final, la primera mitad fue terrible. Y no es la primera vez. Sorprendió el riesgo asumido por el PSV. Tanto que cogió a contrapié a un Madrid repleto de rotaciones. Especialmente en defensa, con Rüdiger y Militao en el eje. A pares por toda la pradera del Bernabéu, los neerlandeses sumaron tres acciones de gol en diez minutos. La primera, por movilidad, no llegó Mijnans a cabecear el centro envenenado de Perisic. La segunda, por velocidad, Van Bommel dejó atrás a Militao, se plantó ante Courtois y remató al lateral de la red. Y la tercera, por osadía, se la apuntó Sergiño Dest, que superó con facilidad a su par, trazó la diagonal y remató al costado de la portería. Quedó claro pues que no era de esos días en que el Madrid se toma el asunto con rigor de inicio. Tampoco ayuda ese 4-3-3 con Diomande, Mbappé y Vinicius en ataque, ante la ausencia de Bellingham, que lo había jugado todo hasta la fecha. Por mucho que trabaje el marfileño, la inferioridad es manifiesta sin balón, y más ante un adversario con buen pie como el PSV. En su reválida personal, Vini quiso liderar la reacción. Estrelló en la cruceta en una diagonal de las suyas. Y facilitó con un estupendo primer toque el dos contra uno de Mbappé y Arda. Tocó mal Kylian y se fue al limbo la ocasión. Era el minuto 14 y parecía que cambiaba la película. Ya. Empezó a recuperar la pelota prontísimo el PSV, por su ambición defensiva y por la falta de futbolistas que se ofrecieran en largo para lucharla, bajarla, jugar de espaldas. Y combinaron los neerlandeses, con sus volantes indetectables. Probó Sano de lejos, pero fue Mijnans quien rompió la baraja. Combinó con Van Bommel, buscó línea de fondo y recibió el pisotón imprudente de Tchouaméni en área. No lo vio Eskas en directo pero corrigió el VAR. Perisic, socio eterno de Modric en la generación dorada de Croacia, transformó el penalti y desató aún más al PSV, dueño y señor del partido. Perdonaron Van Bommel y Sano, solo en el área para el cabezazo. Y el Bernabéu señaló a Vinicius y Mbappé por su falta de intensidad, de coraje, de rebeldía. Lo mínimo, vaya. Perdían muchas. Casi todas. Y se quedaban mirando. No podía ni sospecharse lo que estaba por venir. El correctivo fue tan serio que Mourinho asumió su apuesta fallida con triple cambio al descanso. Relevó a los dos centrales para defender hacia adelante y aclarar la salida del juego y, sobre todo, ingresó Bellingham, que lo primero que hizo fue servir un primer toque primoroso para dejar solo a Valverde. El centro del uruguayo fue tan tenso que no llegó por media talla. Con Arda y Bernardo en el doble pivote, el Madrid fue un huracán. Se contagiaron todos, el primero el turco, que facilitó el empate con un primer toque sutil para la llegada de Valverde, el falso lateral capaz de dominar el juego desde atrás. Pudieron anotar Vini, Bellingham con una tijera espectacular, Diomande, Mbappé, pero era de justicia que quien rompiera la baraja fuese Jude. Acompañó el ataque, controló al aire, se dio el autopase por arriba y desde la frontal conectó la volea con el exterior, cruzada, imposible. Un gol extraordinario para un futbolista descomunal. No se quedó ahí el equipo blanco, incontenible con viento a favor. No había ni rastro del PSV desde que Perisic se quedara en el vestuario. Con el Madrid desbocado aparecieron las carencias del cuadro neerlandés, especialmente en la salida. Estuvo a punto de liarla Geertruida, pero el pecado cayó en la cuenta de Sano, que regaló la pelota a Arda y el turco regaló el tercero a Mbappé. No se contuvo el Madrid, exacto en todos los sectores. Incluso al corregir desventajas como la de Konaté ante Van Bommel. La goleada era inevitable. Entraron Camavinga, que debió ser expulsado por una plancha temeraria, y Brahim. No tuvo minutos Espí, pese a su portada ante el Celta. Pero Mou tiene ángel, y Díaz sirvió un balón perfecto para que Mbappé recordase a Ronaldo Nazario. Regate en largo y 4-1. No se vayan todavía, aún hay más. Porque Bellingham volvió a zidanear con un pase a Vini, que había errado un par de ocasiones claras, y completó la manita. Jude corrió como un poseso a abrazar al 7, y tras él, el grupo entero. Se debe hacer de querer el brasileño. Bien está lo que bien acaba. Y para aspirar a todo, Junior será necesario. Mientras tanto, en la BMV, Jude es el Rey.

articles.title: Lo de cambiar a los centrales había que verlo... y Mou lo vio clarísimo
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Real Madrid - PSV
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Real Madrid - PSV
articles.body: Detectar que el problema del equipo está en los dos centrales y cambiar a ambos al descanso es de muy buen entrenador. Eso hizo Mourinho ante el PSV. Dio entrada a Huijsen y Konaté por Militao y Rüdiger, cambió el rumbo del partido y anuló a un equipo neerlandés que había firmado una primera parte sobresaliente. Pocos habrían apostado por ese doble cambio. Pero el portugués lo tenía claro y con los cambios el Madrid protagonizó los mejores minutos de fútbol en mucho tiempo. Se podría decir que hasta años. También acertó Mou al dar entrada a Bellingham por Tchouaméni. Jude le regaló al Bernabéu los mejores veinte minutos de fútbol de la temporada y se llevará, con razón, los aplausos. Pero la remontada empezó atrás. Con los centrales más agresivos, el Madrid adelantó las líneas y acabó convertido en un vendaval. Un 10 para Mou, que está construyendo un equipo favoritísimo para la Champions. Y ahora, lo de Bellingham. ¡Qué segunda parte! Saltó al campo y firmó una de sus mejores actuaciones con la camiseta del Real Madrid. Jude estuvo por todas partes. Se asoció con todos, aceleró el juego cada vez que recibió la pelota y mezcló intensidad con una finura que se vio, sobre todo, en el gol. ¡Qué golazo! Fue una acción zidanesca. Dos toques para domar el balón y un remate con el exterior para levantarlo por encima del portero. Así cerró Bellingham una noche maravillosa en la que el Bernabéu estaba deseando que entrara en contacto con la pelota. Qué recital. Junto con Bellingham, las acciones más bonitas del partido las firmó Güler. La remontada empezó con un taconazo suyo para que Valverde mandara el balón a la red. Fue una caricia a la pelota, un pase medido para que Fede hiciera el 1-1 con un disparo ajustado al poste. En pleno vendaval del Madrid, Arda también sacó lo mejor de su repertorio y dejó otra asistencia a Mbappé antes de irse al banquillo a descansar. El francés se sumó a la remontada con un doblete en la segunda parte. Ya lleva seis goles en cinco partidos de esta Champions, sin faltar a su cita con el gol en un solo encuentro. Ha marcado en los cinco partidos. Un gol ante Inter, Roma, Leipzig y AEK. Doblete ante el PSV, siendo letal en el mano a mano. Lo que se espera de Mbappé. Ya ha marcado 19 goles en lo que llevamos de temporada. En 18 partidos. A ritmo de Cristiano. El PSV se llevó cinco goles, pero no es mal equipo. Su puesta en escena en la primera parte fue fantástica, con un Ruben van Bommel estelar. Sí, el hijo del mítico de Van Bommel (el holandés del Barça que cosió a patadas a Iniesta en la final del Mundial) dejó una impresión fantástica en el Bernabéu, volviendo loco a Militao en la primera parte. De velocidad endiablada, fue una pesadilla para el Madrid en la primera parte. En la segunda, desapareció, como todo el equipo... Lo engulló el Madrid. Volvió a marcar Vinicius, que no lo hacía desde el 26 de agosto (qué bonita fecha), para terminar de redondear la noche perfecta del Real Madrid. El brasileño fue de menos a más en el partido, como todo el equipo, y terminó cerrando la goleada con un tanto que le devolvió la sonrisa. La celebración de sus compañeros confirmó que Vini lo está pasando mal esta temporada, como el hecho de que Mbappé le cediera su premio de MVP. Todos haciendo piña con el brasileño. Incomprensible, por cierto, que el MVP no fuera para Bellingham.

articles.title: Una maraMilla mantiene flotando al Como
articles.standfirst: El ex del Getafe firmó el gol de la victoria contra el AEK
articles.summary: El ex del Getafe firmó el gol de la victoria contra el AEK
articles.body: En la Champions, como en la Serie A, el Como de Fàbregas se está haciendo grande a una velocidad de vértigo. Y lo demuestra en noches como esta, en las que no brilla, pero aun así encuentra la manera de ganar. Así lo hacen los grandes. No fue una noche de récord, pero le valió la cuarta victoria en cinco jornadas de Champions y el tercer puesto provisional, por detrás del Real Madrid y del PSG. Hace unos años, nadie en Como se habría atrevido ni a soñarlo. En la primera mitad no se vio, ni mucho menos, al Como espectacular de las noches europeas del Sinigaglia. El equipo de Cesc no encontró su habitual ritmo envolvente, ni con balón ni sin él, ante un AEK encerrado con líneas muy juntas y mucha densidad por dentro. El primer disparo local no llegó hasta el 24': Nico Paz se zafó de su par con su control bailón marca de la casa, pero su disparo, ojo, murió en las manos de Strakosha. En el 27' pudo llegar el punto de inflexión. Valle, muy pillo, se ganó un penalti al anticiparse con un estirón a Lovro Majer tras un rebote, pero Da Cunha resbaló sobre el césped empapado y lo mandó fuera. Los griegos, compactos atrás, supieron respirar con el balón gracias a su superioridad numérica en la medular, un quebradero de cabeza para la presión, habitualmente asfixiante, de los de Fàbregas. En el 42' el equipo de Nikolic rozó la campanada por partida doble, pero Martínez estuvo atento ante Gacinovic y Rota. En la reanudación, el Como salió igual: apagado, nervioso e impreciso. En el 51', tras un pase filtrado de visionario de Majer, el auténtico mago griego, Vitalis la mandó por encima desde una posición escorada. Pero, en el momento más delicado, apareció una joya de Luis Milla, el veterano que ha llegado a la Champions con 32 años. Tras la dejada de Baturina, el español se acomodó el balón con el interior y se sacó de la chistera un derechazo con rosca que se coló por la escuadra. En el 60', el Como rozó el segundo: Perrone verticalizó al instante para Nico Paz, que dejó vendido a Strakosha al primer toque, pero el balón lamió el poste. Tras el gol, el Como subió una marcha y tomó el control con autoridad. En el 73', Nico Paz desafió las leyes de la física y se fue de medio AEK antes de mandarla fuera. En el 80', el Sinigaglia respiró aliviado con un cabezazo de Moukoudi a balón parado que se marchó fuera por centímetros. El Como volvió a ganar y firmó la primera portería a cero de su historia europea. Además de Milla, los mejores fueron otros dos españoles. Jacobo Ramón, dominante en los duelos e impecable en la salida de balón, y Álex Valle, siempre incisivo y un tormento constante. En la próxima jornada, la joven legión española de Cesc visitará al Betis en La Cartuja.

articles.title: Pietuszewski reactiva al Oporto para lograr el segundo triunfo seguido
articles.standfirst: Lo necesitaba el conjunto portugués, al que le queda jugar con Liverpool, Slavia Praga y LASK
articles.summary: Lo necesitaba el conjunto portugués, al que le queda jugar con Liverpool, Slavia Praga y LASK
articles.body: En un minuto y 58 segundos, una carrera por el extremo de Oskar Pietuszewski marcó la diferencia en el estadio De Kuip de Róterdam para dar tres puntos fundamentales al Oporto e incidir en las dudas del Feyenoord, con tan solo tres puntos de quince posibles por los seis que suma el conjunto luso, apurado hasta el pitido final (0-1). Lo necesitaba el Oporto, al que le queda jugar con Liverpool, Slavia Praga y LASK, como el Feyenoord, que tiene aún que medirse al Viking, al Galatasaray y al Leipzig, en la competencia de los dos por entrar dentro del corte de 24 equipos que disputarán las eliminatorias a partir del próximo mes de marzo. Es un paso adelante del Oporto. Es un paso atrás del Feyenoord. Todo lo condicionó un gol tan rápido. La primera ocasión, antes de llegar al minuto 2, ya fue gol para el Oporto. Mucho mérito de Oskar Pietuszewski, desbordante hasta la línea de fondo, con el intencionado centro hacia atrás y adentro del área, tan metódico siempre, que Targhalline remató hacia su propia portería ante la llegada de Frodholt. Pietuszewski fue el origen de todo. Tiene 18 años, vuela por el extremo izquierdo y atrae a los grandes clubes de Europa. Su acción tan decisiva incide en ello. El internacional polaco, nacido en 2008, es una realidad ya irrebatible. Su valor de mercado es de 25 millones de euros. El Bayern lo observa con detenimiento para su futuro, tras menos de un año en el club luso, al que llegó en enero de 2026 y con el que ha jugado ya una veintena de partidos. Su evolución es firme. También promovió el siguiente remate de Santiago Giménez, que se reencontró con el equipo neerlandés, en el que despuntó, brilló y fue traspasado al Milan, que lo tiene cedido ahora al Oporto. Su remate de media chilena, un poco alto, lo sirvió también Pietuszewski, antes de cambiar un gol y una ocasión por la necesidad de defenderse del dominio de los locales, cada vez más insistentes. Diogo Costa intervino ante Moussa para proteger el 0-1 a su favor. Se marchó Santiago Giménez del terreno de juego, ovacionado y homenajeado por la que fue su afición, a la hora de partido, aún con el 0–1 a favor del conjunto luso, que sostenía su ventaja al filo, pero realmente sin apenas ocasiones claras del Feyenoord. Al conjunto neerlandés le faltó lo más importante de todo: el pase preciso en los últimos metros, el remate decisivo. Hasta el borde del área llegó con relativa asiduidad, pero apenas creó peligro de verdad. Por eso, Gio Van Bronkhorst introdujo en el campo a Nacho Ferri. Se fue Shaqueel Van Persie, el hijo de Robin Van Persie. En el otro área, Samu Omorodion, a la media vuelta, insistió en la búsqueda del 0-2, en un momento incierto del encuentro. Otra parada de Diogo Costa replicó a la siguiente oportunidad del Feyenoord. Su mano derecha despejó el derechazo de Zechief, igual que Kastenmeier evitó el 0-2. El larguero negó el 1-1 primero, el poste también lo hizo después, incluso un fallo electrónico en el reloj del árbitro indicó que un balón que no había entrado había rebasado la línea de gol. Lo corrigió el VAR entre el alivio del Oporto, reactivado en la Liga de Campeones. Fue la ocasión final.

articles.title: Mourinho: "El vestuario es como Las Vegas, lo que pasa en Las Vegas se queda en Las Vegas"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Real Madrid destaca el partidazo de Bellingham y admite que el PSG les dio "un baño" en el primer tiempo
articles.summary: El entrenador del Real Madrid destaca el partidazo de Bellingham y admite que el PSG les dio "un baño" en el primer tiempo
articles.body: José Mourinho ha destacado el partido del Real Madrid en la segunda parte con los cambios y la aportación de Bellingham en los micrófonos de Movistar. También dejó claro que lo que se dijo en el descanso se queda en el vestuario, comparándolo con Las Vegas. Después, en la sala de prensa, recordó que Jude es el mejor jugador del mundo del medio campo y que no se entiende que no estuviera ni siquiera entre el top ten del Balón de Oro. Jude Bellingham: "Ha hecho un partido absolutamente devastador, ha cambiado el partido, ha hecho un golazo, ha hecho un gol fantástico, hay jugadores que después de los partidos sienten fatiga, pueden jugar pero he pensado quizás mal, he pensado que podía ganar sin él y he intentado protegerlo al máximo, pero tengo un banquillo extraordinario y tenerlo ahí era clave". El cambio de los dos centrales: "Un poco de todo, teníamos amarillas con Tchouaméni y Rüdiger en un partido en el que ellos han tenido transiciones, salían con jugadores rápidos, era un riesgo tener jugadores con amarillas en el campo, es obvio que los dos centrales que están jugando más están con más ritmo e intensidad. He pensado que eran cambios que nos podían arreglar". La charla al descanso: "El vestuario es como Las Vegas, lo que pasa en Las Vegas se queda en Las Vegas. Hemos hablado, somos amigos y hemos hablado". Un Madrid líder en Champions: "15 puntos está muy muy bien, estamos casi ahí, con tres o máximo cuatro no jugamos el playoff, es importante seguir esta racha de victorias. El segundo tiempo es mentalidad, hemos hecho un par de cambios, Jude es un jugador diferente, que nos da lo que no hemos tenido en el primer tiempo pero colectivamente el equipo ha estado mejor. En el primer tiempo no ha encontrado ritmo, no ha presionado, no ha ganado duelos individuales, no ha creado superioridades arriba y en el segundo tiempo hemos presionado alto, línea defensiva muy alta, creo que el PSV no ha logrado salir nunca de su campo con balón limpio como en el primer tiempo". Las palabras de Bellingham: "es simpático al decir esto, no es lo que pienso, el principal responsable es Jude y sus compañeros. Yo intento ayudar un poquito. Es un jugador extraordinario, lo tiene todo: visión, táctica, lo tiene todo y hoy no él solo pero ha cambiado la dirección del partido. Para mí es el mejor jugador del centro del campo del mundo, puede jugar de 10, de 8, por eso cuando se habló del Balón de Oro el escándalo es que no estuviera en el top ten". Lo que ha pasado en la charla al descanso: "he visto el primer tiempo, malísimo, y he intentado con los analistas encontrar tres o cuatro imágenes con las cosas que estábamos haciendo mal. Una imagen vale más que mil palabras y con eso es mucho más fácil para ellos entender. Más que el cambio de los centrales creo que ha sido más que Bernardo y Güler ha sido clave. El PSV nos han dado un baño y en la segunda parte, cuando la gente de arriba se despierta, puede pasar lo que ha pasado". Lo que no le ha gustado: "Hay mucho que pulir, empezar mal los partidos es un problema que tengo yo que solucionar, lógico que acabar ganando es otra cosa y significa que has hecho cosas bien para cambiar, pero con los riesgos que estamos corriendo te puede ir mal. No quiero tener esta sensación". Bellingham como líder: "Sí, es un líder natural porque tiene una autoexigencia muy grande, no es capaz de esconder la frustración pero la combate con trabajo y con el liderazgo de meter el motor a funcionar y todos empezaron a funcionar de un modo totalmente distinto".

articles.title: Erling Haaland frustrated with Manchester City form: 'When you don't win, you question everything'
articles.summary: Erling Haaland said Manchester City's form is 'not good enough' after a run of one win in seven games; Next up for Manchester City is a trip to the Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Rayan Cherki's late strike salvaged a draw but Enzo Maresca's side again struggled to find their fluency.

The draw leaves City in sixth spot in the Champions League table but they are likely to drop out of the top eight by Wednesday evening and have now gone 10 games without a clean sheet. Maresca's men look vulnerable ahead of the trip to Arsenal on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

Haaland speaking to TNT Sports said: "We tried to push but we couldn't. It's not good enough. We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want. Football can be so difficult and easy. When you win games everything is easy and you know exactly what to do, when you don't win you start to question everything. The perfect thing would be to don't think, but it's difficult in these moments.

"We have so much quality. It's about getting that quality out of every single player. We have to regroup to stay positive and bring the energy on the pitch.

"We go to the champions next. The most difficult game of the season. We need a top, top performance."

Maresca: We are conceding too many goals

Ruben Dias was given the night off against Napoli as it was Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol that started together as the centre-back pairing for the first time this season.

Stability is proving elusive for City. Maresca has used eight different back four combinations across City's last 10 games in all competitions, changing his defensive personnel from one game to the next throughout that run.

Not a single clean sheet has been forthcoming and they have conceded 20 goals in that period.

Maresca said: "It's a big game on Sunday. The players have confidence. We don't like these moments when we don't win games, we all want to win games. But unfortunately we need to be patient, to learn and move on.

"We are conceding too many goals. It's quite clear. It's something we need to adjust. We are able to adjust it."

Analysis: Haaland's frustrations reflect Man City's wider problems

"Move the ball quicker," yelled one fan from behind the press box. "Press them," screamed a youngster in front. They were not wrong. Manchester City still have the individual quality to entertain the Etihad Stadium but they are also a frustrating watch at present.

City have picked up just one point from their last four Premier League games and while they did defeat RB Leipzig 3-2 in their previous Champions League outing, they let in two more in this draw with Napoli. It is 10 games now without keeping a clean sheet.

"Off the ball, the team was good from my point of view," said Maresca in the press conference afterwards, presenting a positive spin. "We did not concede a lot. The problem is that they were clinical. We created many chances." Not everyone agreed.

Haaland's assessment that this was "not good enough" and that City were "unable to control or attack the game" chimed more with the feeling inside the stadium. The line that "when you do not win you start to question everything" will resonate.

Maresca is being questioned. He has stressed that he is months into his time here, not years and it is evident that he is still searching for the solutions. Finding the best role for new signings Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez is something that he is still tweaking.

Against Napoli, it was Jeremy Doku's spark off the bench that helped to bring the first equaliser and Rayan Cherki's class that delivered the second. But it was all the bits in between, with and without the ball, that will concern the Manchester City supporters.

Rasmus Hojlund got the better of Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma as Napoli were rewarded for pressing City high up the pitch. Noa Lang converted Leonardo Spinazzola's right-wing cross on the counter-attack - highlighting another weakness.

Maresca turned on his heels and looked to the skies in exasperation at that one because it is a recurring issue for City. They remain susceptible to the breakaways even when he loads the midfield in attempt to prevent it. Losing duels is another theme.

Sluggishness is an easy accusation. Haaland was largely anonymous, unable to get into the game. But that is because City are yet to find a pressing structure that works for them. Even if Haaland does close down, his team-mates are not necessarily following.

As had happened against Fulham at the weekend, Napoli were able to have good possession of the ball, something that was once unheard of for visiting teams at this stadium. That aura was already fading under Pep Guardiola but it is truly absent now.

Maresca is an excellent coach and the structure at Manchester City remains such that he can expect to be given time to figure all this out. But as he himself has previously acknowledged, there is not just one thing that is undermining this team right now.

The loss at Aston Villa was not the same as the home reverse to Brighton. Fulham approached it very differently to Nottingham Forest. Both got results. And now Napoli, in just one game, showed two different ways to undo Maresca's side.

articles.title: Arsenal and Manchester City's problems analysed as both set to meet in bumper Premier League clash this weekend
articles.summary: Arsenal and Man City both slipped up in the Champions League in midweek ahead of their big Premier League meeting this weekend; watch Arsenal vs Man City live on Sky Sports Premier League this Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm
articles.body:
Arsenal have drawn back-to-back games against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund, with Mikel Arteta's side throwing away comfortable half-time leads in both matches.

City, meanwhile, come into the game on a run of just one win in their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

The game could have a huge impact on the Premier League title race, with Arsenal hoping to open up a nine-point lead over Enzo Maresca's side, who in turn could close the gap to the reigning champions to just three points with a win.

Sky Sports reporters Sam Blitz and Adam Bate were at Arsenal and City's draws in midweek and analyse their respective issues...

Arsenal showing bluntness in attack again

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at the Emirates Stadium:

Arsenal have the most 1-0 wins out of any Premier League team since Mikel Arteta took over the club in December 2019. It's all well and good - until teams start making it 1-1.

And in the last two games, they have. And Arsenal only have themselves to blame.

After the Gunners' 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, Arteta was convinced that their recent draws against Newcastle and the Bundesliga leaders are not comparable.

He claims Arsenal played well in this Champions League stalemate - and repeated on several occasions that Dortmund benefited from an "element of luck". There's an element of truth to that - the woodwork was struck three times in the second half.

But Arsenal had thirty shots against Dortmund - the most they've ever had in a Champions League game. Just four of those shots were on target. Seven shots came from within the six-yard box, no goals came from them.

And it's costing them points. Because there has been a pattern in Arsenal's last two matches. Dominate the first half, only take a 1-0 lead, start the second half slowly and then end up drawing the game.

Out of the 2.2 worth of Expected Goals Arsenal missed in the game, 0.96 of that tally came in the first half. From their 13 shots that didn't lead to a goal, they should have taken a bigger advantage.

It invited Dortmund back into the contest when there shouldn't have been one in the first place. Like Newcastle did at the weekend, the Bundesliga leaders sorted their game plan out in the half-time break and came out firing.

Arteta is right that the Newcastle and Dortmund games are different because Arsenal rallied to seize dominance of the game right after the German side's equaliser.

But once again, the conversation sits around the holes in Arsenal's attacking quality, particularly at left wing and up front. After Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus left the club this summer without being replaced, Arsenal are still searching for attacking inspiration at left wing, with neither centre-forward in a goalscoring run of form.

Christos Tzolis is still waiting for his first Arsenal goal, Eberechi Eze is lacking consistency and Viktor Gyokeres backed up his early strike and impressive all-round display by creating doubts again by missing a late sitter.

At the start of the season, Gary Neville questioned whether Arsenal had the attacking player capable of delivering the Champions League. The draw to Dortmund backed that claim up.

Arteta struck a calm and positive tone after the Dortmund draw. It was a figure who knows his team have a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League, and will go on to qualify for the knockout stages of the Champions League.

But if these traits continue, it can all slip away quickly in this busy part of the season. If Arsenal don't beat Real Madrid, their top eight spot will be under threat.

Last season, they also benefited hugely from getting a top two spot that meant the second legs of their entire knockout stages were at the Emirates. PSG and Real can open up a bit of a gap on Arsenal in the coming weeks.

And up next, it's Manchester City at the Emirates. Enzo Maresca's side tend to score in most games. A 1-0 lead may not be enough.

Maresca still searching for the Man City solutions

Sky Sports' Adam Bate at the Etihad Stadium:

Move the ball quicker, yelled one fan from behind the press box. Press them, screamed a youngster in front. They were not wrong. Manchester City still have the individual quality to entertain the Etihad Stadium but they are also a frustrating watch at present.

City have picked up just one point from their last four Premier League games and while they did defeat RB Leipzig 3-2 in their previous Champions League outing, they let in two more in this draw with Napoli. It is 10 games now without keeping a clean sheet.

"Off the ball, the team was good from my point of view," said Enzo Maresca in the press conference afterwards, presenting a positive spin. "We did not concede a lot. The problem is that they were clinical. We created many chances." Not everyone agreed.

"It is not good enough," City captain Erling Haaland had told TNT Sports just before. "We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want." Tellingly, the striker then added: "When you do not win you start to question everything."

Maresca is being questioned. He has stressed that he is months into his time here not years and it is evident that he is still searching for the solutions. Finding the best role for new signings Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez is something that he is still tweaking.

Against Napoli, it was Jeremy Doku's spark off the bench that helped to bring the first equaliser and Rayan Cherki's class that delivered the second. But it was all the bits in between, with and without the ball, that will concern the Manchester City supporters.

Rasmus Hojlund got the better of Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma as Napoli were rewarded for pressing City high up the pitch. Noa Lang converted Leonardo Spinazzola's right-wing cross on the counter-attack - highlighting another weakness.

Maresca turned on his heels and looked to the skies in exasperation at that one because it is a recurring issue for City. They remain susceptible to the breakaways even when he loads the midfield in attempt to prevent it. Losing duels is another theme.

Sluggishness is an easy accusation. Haaland was largely anonymous, unable to get into the game. But that is because City are yet to find a pressing structure that works for them. Even if Haaland does close down, his team-mates are not necessarily following.

As had happened against Fulham at the weekend, Napoli were able to have good possession of the ball, something that was once unheard of for visiting teams at this stadium. That aura was already fading under Pep Guardiola but it is truly absent now.

Maresca is an excellent coach and the structure at Manchester City remains such that he can expect to be given time to figure all this out. But as he himself has previously acknowledged, there is not just one thing that is undermining this team right now.

The loss at Aston Villa was not the same as the home reverse to Brighton. Fulham approached it very differently to Nottingham Forest. Both got results. And now Napoli, in just one game, showed two different ways to undo Maresca's side. Problems to solve.

articles.title: Wyoming football coach Jay Sawvel suspended for season finale for NCAA tampering violations
articles.summary: Sawvel contacted multiple players who were not officially in the transfer portal.
articles.body:
Wyoming coach Jay Sawvel has been suspended for the Cowboys' final game of the regular season.

The school announced Tuesday that it had "worked collaboratively with the NCAA enforcement staff" on the suspension for tampering. In its release, Wyoming said that Sawvel had impermissible communication with seven players who were enrolled at other schools. Those players had announced that they were transferring but had not officially entered the transfer portal.

Wyoming said it self-reported the violations and that it was working with the NCAA on a negotiated resolution. Defensive ends coach Brian Hendricks will serve as the team's head coach against UConn on Saturday.

Wyoming is 7-4 overall and finished its Mountain West schedule at 6-2 following a Week 12 loss to New Mexico. While the Cowboys are currently tied for second in the Mountain West, their two losses were to the Lobos and North Dakota State. Their only hope of making the title game comes down to tiebreakers if Nevada upsets UNLV in Week 13.

Sawvel is in his third season at Wyoming after he was promoted from defensive coordinator following the retirement of Craig Bohl. The Cowboys won just seven games across his first two seasons before guaranteeing a winning record this year with their seventh win of the season.

articles.title: Arteta says Arsenal need more luck to kill off games
articles.summary: Arsenal need more luck to kill off games says manager Mikel Arteta after they are held to a draw by Borussia Dortmund.
articles.body:
It might be emerging more as a theme than as a major problem, but in recent weeks Arsenal cannot seem to finish off matches when they are on top.

In their past nine outings across all competitions, just once have the Gunners won a game by more than a single goal.

The latest frustration came in Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, though perspective is needed. Arsenal might consider it as two points dropped having gone into half-time ahead, but they remain unbeaten in the current Champions League league phase and have not lost at this stage of the competition for more than two years.

But of late, despite dominating large parts of matches, Arsenal have had periods where they have dropped off and allowed opponents back into the game.

Against Slavia Prague away in the Champions League, after scoring twice in the first half, Arsenal 's standards dropped. The same happened against Newcastle in the Premier League last weekend where they found themselves 2-1 behind in the second half having led at the break, before recovering to eventually draw 2-2.

They are producing periods of high-level football, but the struggles to consistently turn that into more goals can lead to nervy finishes.

In the draw with Bundesliga leaders Dortmund, Arsenal had 30 shots but just four of those attempts were on target.

Boss Mikel Arteta mentioned the failure to capitalise post match, though was keen to praise his side's "brilliant performance".

"The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today and what we've done out there, is just something to be very, very pleased [about] because there is very little more that you can demand from the team," Arteta said.

"But obviously, the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance in the amount of chances (and) situations.

"There is an element of luck; there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist because I think what the team has done and shown today, I think it's the right direction."

Arsenal held by Borussia Dortmund in Champions League

Arteta made six changes to the side that drew with Newcastle , with one of the biggest calls to rest striker Kai Havertz and bring in Viktor Gyokeres.

The striker has had a difficult season so far, with four of his seven starts coming in the Champions League against opposition where Arsenal have been favourites.

However, Gyokeres scored a powerful effort from outside the area to give Arsenal the lead against Dortmund.

Overall though, it ended up being a mixed night for the 28-year-old as he missed a header from inside the six-yard-box that would have surely won the game for the Gunners late on.

Arteta was asked if the chances his side are missing were down to mentality, misfortune or composure.

"There is an element of luck here because how some of the goals they haven't gone inside, I don't know.

"The execution can be better, but everything that is in between that, I think it was really, really good."

Arteta was also full of praise for Gyokeres, with particular emphasis on the striker's link-up play; an element of his game at times criticised.

"What I love the most is how connected he was to the team," Arteta said.

"We used him many times in different ways. His link-up play, the way he held the ball, the way he threaded in behind and stretched the pitch.

"There was a lot to like in that performance and that's the Viktor that we needed."

Noni Madueke has been Arsenal 's best attacker in recent weeks.

The winger, who was left out of the last England squad, is enjoying a run in the Arsenal starting XI with Bukayo Saka out injured and is taking his opportunity.

Madueke has registered a goal and two assists in his past three games and was again the best Arsenal forward against Dortmund.

The Gunners host Manchester City on Sunday and are currently six points clear at the top of the Premier League table.

Madueke, who was frustrated with the performance against Dortmund, said the clash with third-placed City is a great chance to get back to winning ways and shake off any frustration.

"I think these are the best games. I'm really looking forward to it. Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same," Madueke told Amazon Prime.

"We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We're champions, we're at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates.

"There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction."
