articles.title: Dabo Swinney Sends Strong Message About South Carolina Star Ahead of Rivalry Showdown
articles.summary: CLEMSON, S.C. — Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney delivered a pointed assessment of South Carolina ahead of Saturday’s Palmetto Bowl, identifying one Gamecocks...
articles.body:
CLEMSON, S.C. — Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney delivered a pointed assessment of South Carolina ahead of Saturday's Palmetto Bowl, identifying one Gamecocks player who could create significant problems for the Tigers.

Speaking during his weekly news conference Tuesday, Swinney discussed the annual rivalry, his relationship with South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer and the challenges awaiting Clemson.

However, his assessment of Gamecocks quarterback LaNorris Sellers stood out as the two programs prepared for another heated meeting.

Dabo Swinney Delivers Message About LaNorris Sellers

Swinney made it clear that Clemson's defensive preparation will revolve around containing Sellers, whose combination of arm strength and mobility presents a difficult matchup.

The Tigers' coach praised the South Carolina quarterback's ability to create explosive plays, even when opposing defenses appear to have favorable positioning.

"Sellers is a problem. He just is," Swinney said Tuesday.

The Clemson coach also emphasized the quarterback's ability to extend plays and threaten defenses with both his arm and legs.

Swinney noted that Sellers can make throws covering 70 yards and produce scoring opportunities from nearly anywhere on the field.

He also acknowledged Clemson's familiarity with the quarterback, whom the Tigers recruited before he committed to South Carolina.

Despite preparing to face him Saturday, Swinney expressed considerable respect for Sellers as both a player and competitor.

The remarks offered a glimpse into Clemson's defensive priorities entering the rivalry matchup.

Clemson Coach Addresses Heated South Carolina Rivalry

Swinney also discussed the emotional nature of the Palmetto Bowl, acknowledging that the rivalry continues to generate intense feelings throughout the state.

Although he maintains relationships with members of South Carolina's coaching staff, Swinney emphasized that those connections do not diminish the importance of winning.

"People still hate each other, so I guess that's good," Swinney said.

The Clemson coach explained that the consequences of losing the rivalry game can linger throughout the following year.

He also distinguished between competing fiercely against an opponent and maintaining personal respect away from the field.

That distinction extends to Beamer, whose Gamecocks have enjoyed recent success at Clemson's Memorial Stadium.

South Carolina won its last two visits to Death Valley, including a 2024 victory that reinforced the rivalry's increasingly competitive nature.

South Carolina Faces Important Rivalry Test

South Carolina (6-5, 4-5 SEC) enters Saturday's contest looking to rebound from a difficult 34-6 loss to Georgia.

The Gamecocks have experienced an inconsistent season, although their offense remains capable of producing explosive plays behind Sellers.

Meanwhile, Clemson (7-4, 5-3 ACC) enters the matchup following a 20-10 victory over Duke.

The Tigers have also dealt with injuries and quarterback uncertainty, creating additional challenges ahead of their regular-season finale.

Nevertheless, Swinney emphasized the importance of finishing the season with a victory over South Carolina.

For the Gamecocks, the matchup provides an opportunity to secure another road victory against their biggest rival.

It also offers Sellers another opportunity to demonstrate his abilities against a prominent nonconference opponent.

Swinney Identifies Another South Carolina Concern

Sellers was not the only Gamecocks player to receive praise during Tuesday's news conference.

Swinney also highlighted South Carolina defensive end Dylan Stewart, whose athleticism and pass-rushing ability present challenges for Clemson's offensive line.

The Tigers' coach praised Stewart's explosiveness, technique and ability to pressure opposing quarterbacks.

He also complimented South Carolina's defensive front, noting its combination of size, strength and speed.

Those comments suggest Clemson expects a physical contest against a Gamecocks defense capable of disrupting both the running and passing games.

South Carolina's ability to pressure Clemson's quarterbacks could become an important factor in determining Saturday's outcome.

Palmetto Bowl Approaches With Plenty at Stake

Saturday's game will mark the 123rd meeting between Clemson and South Carolina.

Kickoff is scheduled for 3 p.m. ET at Memorial Stadium in Clemson, with ESPN2 providing television coverage.

The rivalry has featured a remarkable recent trend, with the visiting team winning each of the past six meetings.

South Carolina will attempt to extend that streak while securing its third consecutive victory at Clemson.

Meanwhile, Swinney and the Tigers will look to end their home struggles against the Gamecocks.

Although Tuesday's news conference featured plenty of discussion about rivalry emotions, Swinney's assessment of Sellers underscored the challenge awaiting Clemson.

The Tigers know which South Carolina player demands their attention.

Whether they can contain him Saturday remains one of the biggest questions entering the Palmetto Bowl.

articles.title: Where will Indiana be in the College Football Playoff rankings? CFP rankings, bracket
articles.summary: Several teams immediately ranked behind Indiana — Tennessee, BYU, Wake Forest and Texas Tech — all won last weekend.
articles.body:
Indiana football fans might not like what they see when the latest College Football Playoff rankings are released Tuesday night, Nov. 24.

The defending national champion Hoosiers (9-2) are in danger of missing the 12-team championship tournament after their overtime loss to Washington last weekend. They also need help to make the Dec. 5 Big Ten title game at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis.

IU was No. 8 in last week's rankings. Several teams immediately ranked behind IU — Tennessee (9-2), BYU (9-2), Wake Forest (10-1) and Texas Tech (10-1) — all won last weekend.

Here's what you should know about tonight's rankings show:

Indiana seeks pivotal win at Washington with CFP, Big Ten title hopes

When will the CFP rankings be released tonight? College playoff rankings start time

The College Football Playoff rankings will be released at 7:30 p.m. ET Tuesday, Nov. 24, or following the Creighton vs. Michigan basketball game.

Where to watch CFP rankings release? College football rankings playoff TV channel

Where to stream CFP rankings release? Stream playoff rankings for college football

Where IU football is projected to rank in the College Football Playoff tonight, Nov. 24

John Talty, CBS Sports, No. 12 : "Sorry, Curt Cignetti, but it's not fake news that your Indiana team is in danger of missing the playoff. The Hoosiers land as the first team out after their loss to Washington. Indiana's resume was already shaky even before the Washington loss, propped up by a single top-25 win over USC. Indiana has a mediocre strength of schedule (No. 41) and hasn't looked particularly good beating the Big Ten's middle class."

Heather Dinich, ESPN, last team in : "The Hoosiers' strength of schedule (No. 40) is slightly better than Texas Tech's (No. 61), and Indiana has been stronger statistically, especially on defense, where the Hoosiers are No. 10 in efficiency. Indiana still has a 51.5% chance to reach the playoff, and a 30.1% chance to reach the Big Ten title game. If Indiana doesn't win the Big Ten and lock up a spot as a Power 4 champ, it would likely be eliminated as a three-loss runner-up. If Indiana finishes as a two-loss team without playing in the conference championship game, its ranking Tuesday night will reveal if the committee thinks the Hoosiers are still worthy of an at-large bid without help from upsets above them."

Nicole Auerbach, NBC Sports, out : "The Hoosiers will likely take a significant tumble after picking up their second loss of the season. Considering that the committee dropped Indiana five spots off a bye, there's no telling what the drop could look like here. The Hoosiers have one top-20 win, but that's about it on the resume. The Hoosiers could be on the wrong side of the cut line based on the way the committee treated Iowa a week ago. The committee put three-loss USC and then three-loss Ohio State ahead of the two-loss Hawkeyes because they had better wins. If that holds, Indiana could definitely be ranked behind the Ducks."

College Football Playoff rankings last week, on Nov. 17

The CFP rankings are revealed each Tuesday until the field is revealed after the conference championship games. The final show will be noon ET Sunday, Dec. 6.

Next week's ranking is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Dec. 1.

How many teams make the College Football Playoffs?

The field is still 12 teams for 2026. It will expand to 24 teams in 2027.

articles.title: Ryan Coleman-Williams ready for his Alabama vs Auburn Iron Bowl moment
articles.summary: Ryan Coleman-Williams' Alabama football dream hinged on the stage the Iron Bowl provides.
articles.body:
Ryan Coleman-Williams ' Alabama football dream hinged on the stage the Iron Bowl provides.

Coleman-Williams is the son of an Auburn defensive back and remembers the Iron Bowls of 2010 and 2011. Coleman-Williams was on the sideline of the 2023 Iron Bowl, watching fourth-and-31: the kind of moment a football player dreams of being a part of.

"I mean, it means everything to me," Coleman-Williams said Tuesday, Nov. 24. "You know, just being an in-state kid, that's all you know. You always have to pick a side."

But while Coleman-Williams knows the Iron Bowl well, he hasn't had his Iron Bowl moment.

As a freshman in Alabama 's 28-14 home win against Auburn in 2024, Coleman-Williams had three catches for 54 yards. As a sophomore in Alabama's 27-20 road win against Auburn in 2025, Coleman-Williams did not receive a target.

When asked about how his 2026 season has gone, a season filled with injuries and adversity, Coleman-Williams said there's "a lot to build on going into this game." When he thinks about the challenges Alabama has faced as a team in 2026, Coleman-Williams said it's all in the context of showing up when it matters most: in the Iron Bowl against Auburn.

Check out our Alabama football vs Chattanooga photo gallery, best images

"Just one of those legacy games that you just get to put your best on the field," Coleman-Williams said.

Coleman-Williams' 2026 season isn't solely defined by his 34 catches, 509 receiving yards or five touchdowns. It's the distraction he poses when healthy, the shiftiness and the potential he poses that forces defensive backs to turn their eyes and allow another receiver to thrive elsewhere. It's his elusiveness that has shown up as a return game.

But to Kalen DeBoer, Coleman-Williams' unwavering leadership and motivation is what defines how important the receiver has been. And with that comes expectation for when Coleman-Williams, once again, steps on the Iron Bowl stage.

"Ryan's gone through it," DeBoer said. "He continues to, I think here at the very end now the last couple weeks, continue to get his body even in a better spot. And I'm looking forward to a big weekend here with him on the football field, helping us lead."

Coleman-Williams knows the stakes. Regardless of the College Football Playoff position, he knows what will happen across the state when he takes the field for his third Iron Bowl.

"I know how many millions of kids are just watching these games and picking their favorite players and dreaming of being in those positions," Coleman-Williams said. "So for me to be here, it's an honor and a blessing."

articles.title: 🤔 Will the Centenario be full? Doubts over the Libertadores final
articles.summary: Carrasco International Airport expects approximately 20,000 arrivals for the Copa Libertadores final between Palmeiras and Estudiantes this Saturday, Novembe...
articles.body:
Carrasco International Airport expects approximately 20,000 arrivals for the Copa Libertadores final between Palmeiras and Estudiantes this Saturday, November 28, at 5:00 p.m. in Montevideo.

Air traffic surges and hotels reach capacity

Nearly 18,000 visitors will arrive between Thursday the 26th and matchday, with more than 30 charter flights and 200 private aviation operations from Argentina and Brazil. With hotels in the capital fully booked, thousands of fans have had to find accommodation more than 150 kilometers away.

History at the Centenario and uncertainty in the stands

The clash is a rematch of the 1968 final at the same venue, with El Pincha seeking their fifth title and Verdão their fourth. Despite reports of a sellout—with 98% of tickets purchased abroad—questions remain over whether the Estadio Centenario will be completely full.
